domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: System Too Lean — E10 Moisture / Fuel Pump Weak
phContext: Toyota Vios (1NR-FE), Mirage (3A92); E10 phase separation in humid monsoon weather
symptoms: Rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, LTFT > +15%
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect STFT/LTFT PIDs at idle vs. 2500 RPM. 2. Check fuel rail pressure (300–350 kPa). 3. Drain fuel sample to check water separation; test fuel pump current draw.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: System Too Rich — Leaking Fuel Injector
phContext: Honda City (L15Z), Toyota Avanza (2NR-VE); prolonged stop-and-go idling
symptoms: Black exhaust smoke, fuel odor in oil, LTFT < -15%
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor O2 B1S1 rich-stuck voltage (>0.8V). 2. Perform fuel pressure leak-down test after key-off. 3. Bench-test injectors for dribble and coil resistance (11–14 ohms).

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire — Foul Fuel or Ignition
phContext: Mitsubishi Xpander (4A91), Suzuki Ertiga (K15B); low-grade or contaminated fuel
symptoms: Flashing MIL, engine shaking at idle, loss of power
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Mode $06 misfire counters per cylinder. 2. Inspect spark plugs for wet fouling or carbon tracking. 3. Scope primary/secondary ignition coils and check fuel pressure.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Cylinder 1 Misfire — Ignition Coil Boot Flashover
phContext: Toyota Vios / Yaris (1NZ-FE / 2NR-FE); engine bay wash or heavy rain splash
symptoms: Single-cylinder shudder under load, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Swap Coil #1 with Coil #2 and check if misfire moves to P0302. 2. Inspect rubber boot for white carbon tracks or moisture. 3. Check 12V, GND, and IGT trigger pulse via oscilloscope.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Cylinder 2 Misfire — Clogged EFI Injector
phContext: Hyundai Accent (Gamma 1.4), Kia Soluto; gummed deposits from short trips
symptoms: Rough idle when cold, stumble on throttle tip-in
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform cylinder drop test via scan tool. 2. Measure injector resistance (12–16 ohms) and noid-light pulse. 3. Ultrasonic clean and flow-test injector #2.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Cylinder 3 Misfire — Worn Spark Plug Electrode
phContext: Toyota Wigo (1KR-FE / WA-VE); overdue 40,000 km tune-up in heavy traffic
symptoms: Vibration at D-gear stop with A/C on, poor fuel economy
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove plug #3 and measure gap (spec 0.8–1.1 mm). 2. Inspect ceramic insulator for hairline cracks. 3. Verify compression (>1100 kPa) if misfire persists.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Cylinder 4 Misfire — Vacuum Leak at Intake Gasket
phContext: Suzuki S-Presso / Celerio (K10B/K10C); heat-aged intake O-rings
symptoms: High idle, misfire at idle that clears at 2500 RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Spray carb cleaner or smoke-test intake runner #4. 2. Check MAP kPa at idle (normal 28–36 kPa). 3. Replace hardened intake manifold gasket.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: MAF Sensor Range/Performance — Oiled Filter / Dust
phContext: Toyota Innova Gas (1TR-FE), Honda Civic; dusty provincial roads or oiled aftermarket filter
symptoms: Sluggish throttle, black smoke on hard acceleration
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare MAF g/s against theoretical displacement at idle (2.0– 4.5 g/s). 2. Inspect hot-wire element for dust/oil film. 3. Clean with dedicated MAF cleaner and retest.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: MAF Sensor Circuit Low Input — Open Signal or 5V
phContext: Mitsubishi Xpander, Nissan Almera; rodent-chewed harness or loose plug
symptoms: Engine stalls immediately after start, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 5V/12V supply and sensor ground at MAF connector. 2. Backprobe signal wire (expect ~0.8– 1.2V key-on/idle). 3. Repair open wire to ECM.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: MAP Sensor Range/Performance — Clogged Vacuum Port
phContext: Honda BR-V / Brio, Suzuki Dzire; oil blow-by residue in manifold
symptoms: Surging idle, delayed transmission upshift
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare Key-On Engine-Off (KOEO) MAP reading with local barometric pressure (~101 kPa). 2. Check vacuum port for carbon blockage. 3. Verify 5V VREF and linear voltage drop under vacuum.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: IAT Sensor Circuit High Input — Open Circuit / Unplugged
phContext: Toyota Vios, Mitsubishi Mirage; forgotten connector after air filter service
symptoms: Hard cold start, slightly rich running, fan stays on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read IAT PID (will show -40°C if open). 2. Check 5V bias on signal pin and ground continuity. 3. Measure sensor resistance (~2.2 kΩ at 25°C).

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: ECT Sensor Circuit Low — Shorted to Ground
phContext: Hyundai Reina, Kia Picanto; chafed wire near thermostat housing
symptoms: Cooling fan runs constantly, rich mixture, gauge maxes out
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ECT PID (shows +140°C if shorted). 2. Unplug sensor; if PID drops to -40°C, sensor is shorted. 3. If still +140°C, trace signal wire for short to ground.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: ECT Sensor Circuit High — Corrosion or Open Wire
phContext: Older Toyota Altis / Vios; coolant seepage onto connector pins
symptoms: Engine cranks long when cold, high idle, radiator fan stuck on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read ECT PID (-40°C indicates open). 2. Jump connector pins; PID should swing to +140°C. 3. Clean green corrosion and verify 5V reference.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: TPS Sensor A Range/Performance — Carbon Track Wear
phContext: Older cable-throttle or early ETC Toyota/Mitsubishi; heavy city pedal cycling
symptoms: Flat spot at 1500– 2000 RPM, erratic AT shifting
diagnosticSteps: 1. Sweep accelerator pedal slowly while scoping TPS1 & TPS2 voltages. 2. Look for dropouts or glitches. 3. Verify TPS1+TPS2 sum equals ~5.0V.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: TPS / ETC Throttle Sensor Low — Pinched 5V VREF
phContext: Nissan Urvan / Almera, Honda Jazz; wiring rub near airbox
symptoms: Engine stuck at 1200 RPM limp mode, no pedal response
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure 5V VREF at throttle body (if <4.5V, unplug other 5V sensors to isolate short). 2. Inspect harness bend near intake boot. 3. Clear codes and perform ETC relearn.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor B1S1 Low Voltage — Exhaust Leak or Lean
phContext: Toyota Vios / Avanza; cracked exhaust manifold gasket from lubak impact
symptoms: Poor fuel mileage, false lean trim correction
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor B1S1 voltage (stuck <0.2V). 2. Add propane to intake; if voltage jumps >0.8V, sensor works and issue is lean/exhaust leak. 3. Inspect manifold-to-cat flange.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor B1S1 No Activity — Poisoned Element
phContext: High-mileage Grab/taxi Toyota Vios; leaded/contaminated fuel or silicone sealant
symptoms: Stuck at ~0.45V bias, sluggish open-loop fuel consumption
diagnosticSteps: 1. Warm engine to 85°C and observe B1S1 switching (must cross 0.1–0.9V). 2. Verify heater circuit 12V and ground. 3. Replace fouled upstream O2 sensor.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor B1S1 Heater Circuit Malfunction
phContext: Mitsubishi Mirage G4, Suzuki Swift; blown heater fuse or open element
symptoms: MIL on immediately at cold start, slow closed-loop transition
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure heater resistance across sensor heater pins (spec 3–15 ohms cold). 2. Test 12V supply at harness with test light. 3. Check ECM heater driver ground pulse.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor B1S2 Heater Circuit — Road Debris Damage
phContext: Low-clearance sedans (City, Vios, Accent); speed bump or flood debris strike
symptoms: MIL on, normal drivability, failed emission test
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect underbody harness near catalytic converter for torn wires. 2. Measure B1S2 heater resistance. 3. Repair wiring with waterproof heat-shrink butt connectors.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: System Too Lean Bank 2 — V6 Intake / PCV Hose Split
phContext: Toyota Fortuner V6 / Camry V6 / Ford Explorer; heat-cracked rubber hoses
symptoms: Rough idle, lean trims on Bank 2, whistling noise
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check LTFT Bank 1 vs. Bank 2. 2. Smoke-test Bank 2 intake runners and PCV hose. 3. Replace split vacuum hose or upper plenum gasket.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Range — GDI High-Pressure Pump
phContext: Ford EcoBoost, Mazda Skyactiv-G, Hyundai GDI; heat soak in traffic
symptoms: Long cranking when hot, engine cuts out above 3000 RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare low-side supply (400–500 kPa) vs. GDI rail pressure PID (3–15 MPa). 2. Inspect high-pressure pump cam follower. 3. Check FRP sensor 5V, GND, and signal.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Injector 1 Circuit Open — Rodent Damage / Loose Clip
phContext: Any PH-parked vehicle; rat chewing injector sub-harness
symptoms: Dead cylinder #1, immediate MIL, strong unburned fuel smell
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure injector #1 coil resistance (11–16 ohms). 2. Check 12V ignition feed at injector plug. 3. Trace ground-side trigger wire back to ECM pin.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit — Burnt Relay or Corroded Ground
phContext: Toyota Vios / Innova, Honda Civic; relay contact pitting from high A/C & traffic load
symptoms: Cranks but no start, no 2-second prime hum at key-on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check EFI/FP fuse and swap fuel pump relay. 2. Backprobe fuel pump connector under rear seat for 12V during crank. 3. Check G-point chassis ground.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit — Overheated Block / Rodent Wire
phContext: Toyota Vios, Honda City, Mitsubishi Xpander; brittle harness under intake
symptoms: Retarded timing, sluggish acceleration, pinging on steep inclines
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect shielded knock sensor wire under intake manifold. 2. Measure sensor capacitance/resistance (typically ~560 kΩ or open piezo). 3. Torque replacement sensor strictly to spec.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: CKP Sensor A Circuit — Oil Leak Fouling or Heat Failure
phContext: Mitsubishi Lancer/Xpander, Hyundai Accent; hot-soak stall in traffic
symptoms: Engine stalls when hot, restarts after 20 min cool-down; no RPM on scan tool
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check RPM PID during crank (0 RPM = CKP fault). 2. Measure Hall/VR sensor supply (5V/12V) or coil resistance (500–1500 Ω). 3. Capture CKP waveform on oscilloscope.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: CMP Sensor A Circuit — Timing Chain Stretch / Sensor Fault
phContext: Nissan Navara/Almera, Toyota 1NR-FE; delayed oil changes in traffic
symptoms: Extended cranking, stalling, rough idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify 5V/12V and ground at CMP connector. 2. Scope CKP vs. CMP phase alignment against OEM waveform. 3. Replace faulty CMP or inspect timing chain tensioner.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary — Overheated Coil Driver
phContext: Honda Jazz/City (L15A/L15Z), Toyota; tropical heat soak under engine cover
symptoms: Intermittent misfire when engine bay is hot, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 12V supply at coil connector under load. 2. Scope IGT trigger signal from ECM (5V square wave). 3. Replace coil if primary current ramp shows shorted turns.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold — Fouled Cat
phContext: High-mileage Vios/City/Mirage; short-trip carbon fouling or oil burning
symptoms: MIL on, normal driving feel, failed LTO/PETC emission HC/CO test
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare B1S1 (rapid switching) vs. B1S2 (steady ~0.6–0.7V) at 2000 RPM. 2. If B1S2 mirrors B1S1, catalyst oxygen storage is depleted. 3. Check for prior misfires or oil consumption.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: EVAP Incorrect Purge Flow — Stuck Purge Solenoid
phContext: Toyota Vios, Honda BR-V, Ford EcoSport; dust/vapor valve sticking
symptoms: Hard start immediately after refueling, rough idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command EVAP purge valve ON/OFF via scan tool and listen for click. 2. Apply hand vacuum to valve; must hold vacuum when de-energized. 3. Check 12V supply and ECM ground pulse.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit — Open Coil
phContext: Mitsubishi Mirage, Suzuki Ertiga; corroded connector near firewall
symptoms: MIL on, fuel vapor odor near hood
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure purge solenoid coil resistance (spec 20–35 ohms). 2. Verify 12V ignition feed at harness. 3. Check continuity of control wire to ECM.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: EVAP System Large Leak — Loose or Cracked Gas Cap
phContext: All OBD-II PH vehicles; worn rubber gasket on fuel cap
symptoms: MIL on after refueling, faint fuel smell near rear quarter
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect fuel cap O-ring for cracks and verify click lock. 2. Smoke-test EVAP system via service port (1 psi max). 3. Check filler neck rust on older coastal vehicles.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Idle Air Control / ETC Idle Fault — Carbon-Clogged Throttle
phContext: Toyota Vios, Mitsubishi Xpander, Suzuki Ertiga; heavy EDSA idling carbon
symptoms: Engine stalls when releasing throttle or turning A/C on, hunting idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check IAC step count or ETC throttle angle PID at idle (normal 2– 4%). 2. Inspect throttle plate bore for heavy black carbon ring. 3. Clean throttle body and perform idle air volume relearn.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Idle Control System RPM Lower Than Expected
phContext: Honda City, Toyota Avanza; high electrical/A/C load with dirty throttle
symptoms: Shuddering at stoplight in D-gear, RPM drops below 550
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check battery voltage under A/C + headlight load. 2. Clean throttle body carbon deposits. 3. Reset ECM learned idle values and relearn.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Idle Control System RPM Higher Than Expected — Vacuum Leak
phContext: Suzuki Ertiga, Hyundai Accent; torn PCV hose or unseated brake booster hose
symptoms: Idle stuck at 1300– 1600 RPM, hard clunk shifting into Drive
diagnosticSteps: 1. Clamp PCV and brake booster hoses briefly to see if RPM drops. 2. Smoke-test intake manifold. 3. Check ETC pedal/throttle zero-point calibration.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: System Voltage Low — Weak Alternator / Bad Ground
phContext: Any PH vehicle in heavy traffic with A/C + audio + dashcam
symptoms: Dim lights, erratic sensor DTCs, transmission limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure battery voltage at idle with full load (must be >= 13.2V). 2. Perform voltage drop test on B+ cable and engine-to-chassis ground (<0.2V). 3. Inspect alternator brushes.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault — Voltage Spike or Water Ingress
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova, Mitsubishi; jump-start polarity reversal or flood dampness
symptoms: No start or erratic multi-system faults, cooling fans maxed
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify all ECM 12V (B+, IG1, MREL) and ground pins under load. 2. Inspect ECM PCB for burned traces or green corrosion. 3. Reflash or replace ECM with immobilizer sync.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Fuel Pump Control Circuit Open — Corroded Tank Harness
phContext: SUVs/MPVs exposed to flood puddles; underbody fuel tank connector
symptoms: Sudden stall while driving, cranks no start
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test 12V and ground at fuel pump module connector during crank. 2. Check fuel pump relay and inertia switch (if equipped). 3. Clean or bypass corroded underbody splice.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Throttle Actuator Control Range/Performance — Sticking Plate
phContext: Nissan Almera, Ford Fiesta, Toyota 2NR-FE; carbon binding or stripped gear
symptoms: Limp mode (max 2000 RPM), EPC/wrench light on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor APP1/APP2 vs. TPS1/TPS2 tracking via scan tool. 2. Inspect throttle motor resistance (2–5 ohms) and H-bridge driver current. 3. Clean bore or replace ETC unit.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: VVT-i / Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced — Sludge
phContext: Toyota Vios/Avanza, Honda i-VTEC; extended oil change intervals in traffic
symptoms: Rattle on cold start, rough idle, stalling at stops
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect engine oil level and sludge on dipstick. 2. Remove OCV (Oil Control Valve) and clean clogged mesh filter screen. 3. Actuate OCV with 12V/scan tool to verify smooth spool movement.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: VVT-i Camshaft Timing Over-Retarded — Stuck OCV
phContext: Toyota 1NR-FE / 2ZR-FE; varnished VVT solenoid
symptoms: Poor low-end torque, sluggish uphill climb, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command VVT solenoid duty cycle via scan tool; observe cam angle PID response. 2. Measure OCV coil resistance (6.9–7.9 ohms at 20°C). 3. Flush oil and replace sticking OCV.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Exhaust Camshaft Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
phContext: Dual VVT-i Toyota Vios/Altis, Kia/Hyundai Dual CVVT
symptoms: Rough idle, fuel economy drop, rattle under light load
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check exhaust OCV filter screen for debris. 2. Compare desired vs. actual exhaust cam phase PID. 3. Inspect cam phaser lock pin wear.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Crank/Cam Correlation Bank 1 — Stretched Timing Chain
phContext: Nissan Navara/Almera, Toyota; overdue oil service
symptoms: Long cranking, rattling timing cover, sluggish power
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope CKP and CMP signals simultaneously and check phase offset. 2. Inspect timing chain tensioner extension. 3. Replace timing chain kit if stretched.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit B1S1 — Blown Fuse / Driver
phContext: Hyundai Accent, Kia Rio; heater short blowing ECM/sensor fuse
symptoms: MIL on, slow warm-up fuel trim stabilization
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Engine/Sensor fuse in engine bay box. 2. Unplug O2 sensor and test heater resistance (no short to ground). 3. Check ECM low-side PWM driver.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit B1S2 — Underbody Splash
phContext: Sedans driving through deep puddles; downstream O2 plug
symptoms: MIL on after heavy rain, normal engine feel
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug B1S2 connector under floorpan and check for water/corrosion. 2. Test heater resistance (4–16 ohms). 3. Dry, apply dielectric grease, and clear DTC.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temp — Stuck Open
phContext: Older Toyota/Honda with thermostat removed by previous mechanic
symptoms: Engine never reaches 85°C, high fuel consumption, stays in warm-up enrichment
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor ECT PID during 15-min drive (stalls at 60–72°C). 2. Feel upper radiator hose—if warm immediately at cold start, thermostat is stuck open or missing. 3. Install OEM 82–88°C thermostat.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor B1S2 High Voltage — Shorted to Heater 12V
phContext: Aftermarket O2 splice errors or melted exhaust wiring
symptoms: B1S2 stuck >1.1V, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read B1S2 PID (normal 0.1–0.9V; >1.1V indicates 12V short). 2. Inspect harness near exhaust pipe for melted insulation. 3. Verify pinout of aftermarket O2 sensor.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: System Too Rich Bank 2 — High Fuel Pressure / MAF Skew
phContext: V6 SUVs/sedans; clogged air filter or faulty FPR
symptoms: Black smoke, fouled plugs, poor mileage
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect air filter for heavy dust/mud clogging. 2. Compare MAF reading against calculated load. 3. Check fuel pressure regulator vacuum diaphragm for raw fuel.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: TPS/Pedal Sensor B Circuit Low — Water in Pedal Connector
phContext: Flooded cabin floorpan vehicles; APP sensor near accelerator pedal
symptoms: No throttle response, stuck at 1500 RPM limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect APP connector at pedal bracket for flood silt/corrosion. 2. Measure 5V VREF and APP1/APP2 voltage sweeps (typically APP1 ~0.7– 4.2V, APP2 ~0.35–2.1V). 3. Replace corroded pedal assembly.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Knock Sensor 1 High Input — Loose Bracket / Harness Short
phContext: Toyota/Mitsubishi gasoline engines; improper torque or pinched wire
symptoms: MIL on, sluggish timing advance
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect knock sensor connector for bent pin or moisture. 2. Check signal wire for short to 5V/12V. 3. Verify sensor mounting surface is clean and torqued to spec.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Gasoline EGR Flow Insufficient — Carbon-Blocked Passage
phContext: Honda City/Jazz i-DSI & i-VTEC, Hyundai; city idling soot
symptoms: Engine pinging/knocking on light acceleration, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command EGR valve open at idle via scan tool (engine should stumble/stall). 2. If no RPM change, remove EGR valve and clean carbon from intake ports. 3. Check EGR pintle position sensor.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: EVAP Vent Control Circuit — Mud-Clogged Canister Vent
phContext: Crossovers/sedans driving on muddy provincial roads
symptoms: Gas pump nozzle clicks off repeatedly during refueling, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect charcoal canister vent valve under rear chassis for mud/insect nest blockage. 2. Test 12V and ground actuation of vent solenoid. 3. Blow out vent line with low-pressure air.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Vehicle Speed Sensor A — Rat-Chewed Wire / ABS Fault
phContext: Older Toyota Vios/Innova without ABS, or ABS-derived speed signal
symptoms: Speedometer drops to zero, erratic shifting, power steering heavy
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check VSS/wheel speed PIDs while driving. 2. Inspect 3-wire Hall VSS on transmission or ABS module CAN speed output. 3. Repair damaged harness.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Power Steering Pressure Sensor — Leaky Switch
phContext: Hydraulic-PS Toyota Innova/Vios/Avanza; fluid seeping through switch
symptoms: Engine stalls when turning steering wheel at idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor PSP switch PID while turning wheel lock-to-lock (must toggle OFF/ON). 2. Check connector for PS fluid contamination. 3. Replace leaking pressure switch.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Starter Relay Circuit — Burned Starter Solenoid / Relay
phContext: High-mileage taxis/TNVS units; frequent stop-start cycles
symptoms: No crank at key turn, relay clicks or silent
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Park/Neutral safety switch PID. 2. Test ST relay coil 12V/GND and output to starter S-terminal. 3. Check voltage drop on main battery-to-starter cable.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Open — Main Relay Failure
phContext: Toyota EFI Main Relay, Honda PGM-FI Main Relay; heat soak
symptoms: No-crank or cranks-no-start, no MIL at Key-On, scan tool cannot connect
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if MIL illuminates at KOEO. 2. Test EFI/Main Relay coil and contact terminals for heat-induced open circuit. 3. Verify ignition switch IG1 feed to ECM.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Startability Malfunction (Toyota) — Weak Battery / Fuel Drain
phContext: Toyota Vios/Avanza/Innova; marginal battery or dirty throttle
symptoms: Extended cranking before firing, stored history code
diagnosticSteps: 1. Load-test battery (cranking voltage must stay >= 9.6V). 2. Clean throttle body and MAF sensor. 3. Check fuel pressure hold after overnight soak.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Range/Performance
phContext: Ford Fiesta/EcoSport, Nissan, Toyota; internal motor brush wear
symptoms: Sudden limp mode in traffic, wrench/MIL warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure throttle motor resistance (2–5 ohms) while gently moving plate. 2. Check ECM driver fuse and wiring resistance. 3. Replace ETC body and relearn.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: Throttle Actuator Control Body Range — Sticking Return Spring
phContext: High-mileage ETC vehicles; carbon gum around butterfly edge
symptoms: Delayed return to idle, limp mode triggered
diagnosticSteps: 1. With key off, check smooth spring return of throttle plate. 2. Clean carbon carefully without forcing gears. 3. Verify TPS resting voltage matches spec.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: TPS/Pedal Position Sensor A/B Voltage Correlation
phContext: Mitsubishi Xpander, Nissan, Honda; moisture in throttle plug
symptoms: Immediate limp mode, idle stuck at 1500 RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Graph TPS1 and TPS2 simultaneously; look for divergence or flat-line. 2. Inspect 6-pin ETC connector for fretting corrosion. 3. Check 5V VREF stability.

domainName: Engine Management & Fuel Delivery (Gasoline / EFI / GDI)
title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean B1S1 — Vacuum/Injector
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis, Ford; unmetered air after MAF
symptoms: Rough idle, high positive fuel trims, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Smoke-test intake tract between MAF and cylinder head. 2. Check PCV valve for stuck-open condition. 3. Verify fuel injector flow balance.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure Too Low — Clogged Fuel Filter
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner (1KD/2GD), Montero (4D56/4N15); dirty diesel or overdue filter
symptoms: Engine enters limp mode under overtaking load, hard cold start
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare Desired vs. Actual Rail Pressure PID under load (e.g., 30 MPa idle, 160+ MPa WOT). 2. Inspect primary fuel filter/water separator for wax or algae. 3. Perform injector leak-off (return flow) test.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too High — Sticking SCV
phContext: Toyota D-4D, Mitsubishi 4D56, Isuzu 4JJ1; varnished Suction Control Valve
symptoms: Diesel knock/clatter, surging idle, stall on deceleration
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor rail pressure PID at idle (spikes >45 MPa indicate stuck SCV). 2. Scope SCV PWM duty cycle (normal 30–40% at idle). 3. Replace SCV and perform pump pilot learn.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance — Erratic SCV
phContext: Nissan Navara (YD25), Ford Ranger; worn SCV plunger
symptoms: RPM hunting at idle, intermittent stalling at traffic lights
diagnosticSteps: 1. Graph Rail Pressure vs. SCV current PID; look for +/- 5 MPa oscillation. 2. Check fuel tank pickup screen for debris. 3. Replace SCV and reset ECU fuel pump learn values.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel System Large Leak Detected — Ruptured Return / Seal
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Innova, Isuzu D-Max; cracked injector return hose or relief valve
symptoms: Sudden engine cut-off under acceleration, fuel smell
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect high-pressure lines, common rail relief valve, and return hoses. 2. Perform capped-rail pressure test (isolating injectors). 3. Measure individual injector back-leakage (<30 mL/min).

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Range — Harness Vibration
phContext: Ford Ranger, Isuzu D-Max; loose rail sensor plug from diesel vibration
symptoms: Rough running, erratic rail pressure spikes on scan tool
diagnosticSteps: 1. Wiggle-test FRP sensor harness while watching rail pressure PID. 2. Check 5V VREF, GND, and signal (~1.0V KOEO, ~1.5V idle). 3. Repair pin tension or replace sensor.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High — Open Ground
phContext: Toyota 1KD/2KD, Mitsubishi 4D56; corroded connector or broken ground
symptoms: Engine cranks no start or instant limp mode, PID reads max 200+ MPa
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read FRP voltage PID at KOEO (5.0V indicates open ground or shorted signal). 2. Check sensor ground continuity to ECM. 3. Replace damaged pigtail.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Injector Circuit Malfunction — EDU / Piezo Driver Fault
phContext: Toyota 1KD-FTV / 2KD-FTV (separate EDU box); moisture in EDU plug
symptoms: Engine stalls or runs on 2 cylinders, no injector click
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check EDU power relay and ground. 2. Scope high-voltage injector drive pulse (80–120V spike on piezo/solenoid). 3. Inspect EDU connector for water corrosion.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbocharger Overboost — Seized VGT Vanes (Carbon)
phContext: Mitsubishi Montero/Strada, Toyota 2GD-FTV, Isuzu; short city trips carbon-locking VGT
symptoms: Limp mode at 80– 100 km/h highway climb, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Actuate VGT actuator/solenoid via scan tool and watch linkage travel. 2. Check MAP/boost PID under load (exceeding 240–260 kPa). 3. Clean soot from VGT nozzle ring.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbocharger Underboost — Split Intercooler Hose
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest, Montero Sport, Navara; oil-softened silicone boost hose
symptoms: Black exhaust smoke, whistling sound, sluggish uphill pull
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressurize intake tract from turbo outlet to 100 kPa (15 psi) with smoke/air. 2. Inspect lower intercooler hoses for splits. 3. Check VGT vacuum/electronic actuator operation.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGR Flow Insufficient — Soot-Clogged Intake & Valve
phContext: Toyota Fortuner/HiAce, Montero Sport, Isuzu D-Max; heavy Metro Manila idling
symptoms: Sluggish throttle, black smoke, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command EGR open via scan tool; verify MAF g/s drops as EGR opens. 2. Remove EGR valve and intake elbow to inspect heavy wet soot buildup. 3. Decarbonize intake and verify valve stroke.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGR Flow Excessive — Stuck-Open EGR Valve
phContext: Ford Ranger, Hyundai Starex CRDi; carbon chunk jamming pintle open
symptoms: Heavy black smoke, stalling at idle, no low-end power
diagnosticSteps: 1. Block EGR pipe temporarily with test plate; if idle smooths out, valve is stuck open. 2. Inspect EGR cooler for coolant leaks mixing with soot. 3. Clean or replace EGR valve.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGR Control Circuit Range/Performance — Stepper/DC Motor
phContext: Toyota 1GD/2GD, Mitsubishi 4N15; stripped plastic gear or jammed shaft
symptoms: Limp mode, MIL on, erratic boost
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor Desired vs. Actual EGR Position PID. 2. Measure EGR motor coil resistance and position sensor 5V/GND. 3. Replace EGR actuator assembly.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGR Sensor A Circuit Low — Shorted Position Sensor
phContext: Isuzu 4JJ1, Hyundai Accent CRDi; moisture in EGR cap
symptoms: MIL on, EGR disabled by ECU
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read EGR position voltage PID (<0.2V indicates short to ground). 2. Unplug EGR; if voltage rises to 5V, sensor is internally shorted. 3. Replace EGR assembly.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Glow Plug Module Control Circuit — Blown Glow Fuse
phContext: Ford Ranger, Nissan Navara, Isuzu; shorted glow plug blowing module
symptoms: Hard cold start in Baguio/Tagaytay mornings, white smoke on startup
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check glow plug relay/module main fuse (60–80A). 2. Measure resistance of each glow plug to ground (spec 0.5– 2.0 ohms). 3. Replace shorted glow plug and module.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit — Open Element
phContext: Toyota Hilux/HiAce, Mitsubishi Montero; aged glow plug
symptoms: Rough cold start idle for first 10 seconds, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect glow busbar/connector and test plug #1 resistance to block (<2 ohms). 2. Verify 12V feed during KOEO pre-glow phase. 3. Replace open glow plug.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Pump Over-Pressure / SCV Fault (Nissan)
phContext: Nissan Navara (YD25) / Urvan (NV350); sticky SCV
symptoms: Limp mode, stalling after hard acceleration
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform ECU fuel pump learn reset after replacing SCV. 2. Inspect fuel filter for metal shavings (indicating HP pump wear). 3. Verify rail pressure stability.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbo Stepper Motor Circuit (Toyota D-4D) — Jammed VNT
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner/HiAce 1KD/2KD; carbon-locked VNT ring
symptoms: Sudden limp mode on expressway (SLEX/NLEX), clears on restart
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect VNT linkage and move lever by hand (must move freely). 2. Check VN turbo driver box 12V and CAN/PWM signals. 3. Clean turbo vanes or replace VN driver.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Injector Compensation Code Error — Uncoded Replacement
phContext: Toyota D-4D, Isuzu, Mitsubishi; mechanic replaced injector without coding
symptoms: Excessive diesel knock, black smoke, rough idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read 30-digit (Toyota) or 16/20-digit IMA injector calibration codes via scan tool. 2. Compare against QR/laser code stamped on each injector top. 3. Program exact codes into ECM.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: DPF Efficiency Below Threshold — Cracked Substrate / Hollowed
phContext: Euro-4+ Hilux/Fortuner (2GD), Ford Ranger, Isuzu 4JJ3; traffic soot or tampered DPF
symptoms: Flashing DPF light, high soot load, black tailpipe
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Differential Pressure Sensor PID at idle (<2 kPa) and 2500 RPM. 2. Inspect exhaust tailpipe for black soot (indicates cracked DPF). 3. Check sensor hoses for splits.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Water in Fuel Condition — Contaminated Diesel
phContext: All PH CRDi pickups/vans; underground fuel tank condensation during typhoons
symptoms: Water-in-Fuel warning light on, rough running, injector risk
diagnosticSteps: 1. Immediately drain water separator bowl at primary fuel filter. 2. Test WIF float/conductivity sensor at bottom of filter housing. 3. Flush tank if heavy water/sludge present.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Range — Clogged/Melted Hose
phContext: Ford Ranger, Toyota 2GD-FTV; heat-cracked rubber sensor hose
symptoms: False DPF full warning, forced limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read DPF diff pressure PID at KOEO (must be ~0 kPa). 2. Inspect silicone hoses from DPF to sensor for pinholes or soot blockage. 3. Replace hoses and reset DPF learned values.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: DPF Restriction Soot Accumulation — Failed City Regen
phContext: Euro-4+ PH diesels stuck in EDSA/C5 traffic never reaching regen temp
symptoms: DPF light solid/flashing, limp mode, high engine oil level (fuel dilution)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Soot Mass % PID (if >100– 140%, static regen may be locked out). 2. Check engine oil level for diesel dilution before forced regen. 3. Perform service DPF regeneration or off-car ultrasonic clean.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Diesel MAF Skew — Crankcase Blow-by Oil Coating
phContext: Toyota 2KD/1KD, Isuzu 4JJ1; oil mist from PCV coating MAF
symptoms: Sluggish turbo spool, incorrect EGR calculation
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check MAF g/s at idle (with EGR closed vs. open). 2. Clean MAF element and inspect air filter box for oil pooling. 3. Check PCV separator.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Temp Sensor A Circuit High — Open Sensor in Pump
phContext: Nissan Navara, Mitsubishi 4D56; broken wire at HP pump
symptoms: Hard hot-start, MIL on, inaccurate fuel quantity compensation
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Fuel Temp PID (-40°C indicates open circuit). 2. Measure sensor resistance at HP pump (~2.0– 2.5 kΩ at 25°C). 3. Repair brittle 2-pin pump connector.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A — Worn SCV/IMV
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest, Hyundai Starex; metallic debris in IMV
symptoms: Stalling under load, P0087 companion code
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove IMV/SCV and inspect micro-screen for brass/steel glitter. 2. Scope IMV PWM drive current. 3. Replace IMV and fuel filter (flush system if glitter found).

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance — Worn Copper Injector Seal
phContext: Toyota 1KD-FTV (Hilux/Fortuner 2005– 2015); blow-by past copper washer
symptoms: Cold-start rattle, milky/sludgy oil, clogged oil pickup risk
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Injector Feedback Value (IFV) PIDs at hot idle (spec within +/- 3.0 mm³/st). 2. Remove oil cap at idle; excessive chuffing smoke confirms blow-by past injector seals. 3. Replace all 4 copper seals and inspect oil pickup screen.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Cylinder 2 Contribution/Balance — High Return Flow
phContext: Hyundai Starex, Isuzu D-Max, Ford Ranger; worn injector control valve
symptoms: Rough idle, knocking cylinder #2, black smoke
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check cylinder #2 balance PID (+3 to +5 mm³/st indicates weak cylinder). 2. Run 4-bottle return leak-off test at idle for 2 minutes. 3. Rebuild or replace injector #2.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Cylinder 3 Contribution/Balance — Seized Nozzle Tip
phContext: CRDi vehicles running poor-quality provincial diesel
symptoms: Misfire/knock at cylinder #3, white unburned diesel smoke
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform cylinder cut-out test via scan tool. 2. Compare injector #3 feedback correction. 3. Pull injector #3 for pop/spray-pattern bench testing.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Cylinder 4 Contribution/Balance — Low Compression / Injector
phContext: High-mileage UV Express HiAce / L300; worn rings or injector
symptoms: Excessive cranking blow-by, cylinder #4 imbalance
diagnosticSteps: 1. Swap injector #4 with #1 (re-coding if needed) to see if fault follows injector. 2. Perform relative compression test via starter current clamp on scope. 3. Run manual compression test (spec >2400 kPa).

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGR Control Circuit Low — Shorted EGR Solenoid
phContext: Ford Ranger, Mitsubishi Montero; water in EGR actuator
symptoms: MIL on, fuse blown, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug EGR and check if 12V supply fuse holds. 2. Measure EGR motor windings for short to case. 3. Inspect harness near exhaust heat shield.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGT Sensor 1 Circuit (Bank 1) — Heat Fatigue Open
phContext: Euro-4+ Hilux/Fortuner, Ford Ranger; pre-turbo EGT sensor failure
symptoms: DPF regen inhibited, limp mode, EGT PID stuck at 1000°C or -40°C
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read EGT1 PID at cold key-on (should match ambient ~30°C). 2. Measure sensor resistance (PTC or NTC per OEM spec). 3. Replace open EGT sensor.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: EGT Sensor 2 Circuit High — Broken Wire Under Floor
phContext: Isuzu mu-X/D-Max, Toyota 2GD; off-road/lubak snag on mid-pipe sensor
symptoms: DPF light flashing, failed regen
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect EGT2 sensor wiring above mid-exhaust pipe. 2. Check 5V bias at harness connector. 3. Repair chafed wire or replace EGT2 sensor.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage — Shorted Piezo
phContext: Ford Ranger 2.2/3.2 (SID208), Toyota 1KD; internal piezo/coil short
symptoms: Engine shuts down instantly, cylinders 1 & 4 dead
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure injector resistance AND insulation to cylinder head (must be >10 MΩ at 500V/DMM). 2. Unplug injectors one by one to see which restores ECM driver. 3. Replace shorted injector.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 2 Performance — Relief Valve Leak
phContext: Toyota D-4D, Isuzu 4JJ1; weak common rail pressure limiter valve
symptoms: P0087 under hard pull, fuel returning from rail end
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect return hose from rail pressure limiter valve; zero fuel should exit at idle. 2. If leaking, replace limiter valve and check SCV. 3. Verify rail holds 160+ MPa.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Glow Plug/Heater Circuit A — Burned Relay Contacts
phContext: Mitsubishi L300/Montero, Isuzu Crosswind; high current relay pitting
symptoms: Long cranking in cool mornings, glow light stays off or flashes
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage at glow plug busbar during KOEO (must be >10.5V). 2. Test glow relay contact resistance. 3. Check all 4 glow plugs for open circuit.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: IAT Sensor 1 Range/Performance — Intercooler Heat Soak
phContext: Turbo diesels in crawling traffic; sensor mounted post-intercooler
symptoms: Sluggish throttle after idling, timing retard
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare IAT1 (MAF) vs. IAT2 (manifold) at cold KOEO (must be within 3°C). 2. Clean oil film from intake manifold IAT sensor. 3. Check intercooler fan/airflow.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbo Boost Sensor A Circuit High — Oil-Fouled MAP
phContext: Mitsubishi Montero 4D56, Hyundai Starex; EGR soot + oil clogging MAP
symptoms: Limp mode, MAP PID stuck at 300 kPa
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read MAP PID at KOEO (should be ~101 kPa). 2. Remove MAP sensor from intake manifold and clean oil/soot sludge. 3. Check 5V/GND/signal wiring.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Exhaust Pressure Sensor Range — Soot-Plugged Tube
phContext: Isuzu D-Max, Ford Ranger, Toyota 2GD; clogged metal sensor pipe
symptoms: Erratic turbo boost control, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Exhaust Backpressure PID at KOEO (~101 kPa). 2. Remove sensor and blow out carbon-clogged steel tube. 3. Replace sensor if diaphragm is damaged.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Engine Oil Pressure Too Low — Clogged Oil Pickup Screen
phContext: Toyota 1KD-FTV (Fortuner/Hilux); carbon from leaking injector seals
symptoms: Oil pressure warning light at hot idle, catastrophic bearing risk
diagnosticSteps: 1. DO NOT drive; attach mechanical oil pressure gauge (spec >30 kPa idle, >250 kPa at 3000 RPM). 2. Drop oil pan and inspect pickup strainer for carbon chunks. 3. Fix injector copper seals.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Internal Control Module A/D Processing — Ground Noise
phContext: Diesel pickups with aftermarket HID/LED/winch wired to ECM ground
symptoms: Random phantom sensor codes, momentary stutter
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect aftermarket accessory grounds on battery/firewall. 2. Check alternator AC ripple (<50 mV AC). 3. Clean OEM ECM ground straps.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance — EDU Capacitor
phContext: Toyota 1KD/2KD; aging high-voltage boost capacitor in EDU
symptoms: Hard hot restart, random stall, P062D/P0200
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope EDU boost voltage (typically 85–110V). 2. Inspect EDU PCB for bulged electrolytic capacitors or cracked solder joints. 3. Repair/replace EDU.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: TCM Requested MIL — Diesel Torque Reduction Active
phContext: Montero Sport, Fortuner, Ranger AT; transmission fault limiting boost
symptoms: Engine won't rev past 2500 RPM, AT light flashing
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan TCM for specific transmission DTCs. 2. Check battery voltage and CAN lines. 3. Resolve TCM fault first to restore full engine torque.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Pressure Too Low (Hyundai/Kia CRDi) — Tank Strainer
phContext: Hyundai Starex / Tucson / Accent CRDi; clogged in-tank pre-filter
symptoms: Engine stalls above 2500 RPM, restarts after 1 minute
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check low-pressure lift pump supply or vacuum before HP pump. 2. Pull in-tank sender unit and inspect mesh sock for black algae/slime. 3. Replace spin-on fuel filter.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Injector Trim / EDU Sync Fault (Isuzu 4JJ1/4JK1)
phContext: Isuzu D-Max / mu-X; corroded EDU/ECM harness near wheel well
symptoms: Engine runs rough in limp mode, clattering idle
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check EDU 12V supply and ground under load. 2. Verify injector ID codes stored in ECM. 3. Inspect driver-side fender harness for rub-through.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Low — Swirl Flap Jam
phContext: Ford Ranger, Hyundai CRDi, Mazda BT-50; heavy EGR carbon locking flaps
symptoms: Sluggish low-end torque, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Actuate swirl flap linkage via scan tool; check for mechanical binding. 2. Clean intake manifold carbon buildup. 3. Check IMRC motor/solenoid 12V and ground.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor D Low — Floor Moisture
phContext: Work pickups/vans with muddy boots dripping onto pedal sensor
symptoms: Stuck at idle (750– 1000 RPM), no throttle response
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check APP1/APP2 PIDs while pressing pedal. 2. Dry and clean 6-pin pedal connector. 3. Verify 5V VREF at pedal plug.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbo Boost System Performance — Vacuum Leak at Solenoid
phContext: Mitsubishi 4D56, Nissan YD25; cracked vacuum hoses to VGT/boost solenoid
symptoms: Slow turbo spool, black smoke, underboost
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test vacuum pump output (spec -75 to -90 kPa / 22–26 inHg). 2. Inspect all rubber vacuum lines to VGT actuator and EGR. 3. Test VGT vacuum solenoid duty cycle.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Intake Air System Leak — Cracked Intercooler End Tank
phContext: High-mileage pickups/vans; plastic end-tank crack or blown clamp
symptoms: Loud whooshing noise under boost, high EGT, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressure-test entire charge air cooler circuit at 100 kPa. 2. Spray soapy water on intercooler seams and hose clamps. 3. Replace cracked intercooler or T-bolt clamp.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbo Boost Control Position Sensor Range — VGT Potentiometer
phContext: Ford Ranger 2.2/3.2, Mitsubishi 4N15; worn VGT position sensor
symptoms: Sudden limp mode, wrench light, sluggish boost
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read VGT Position Desired vs. Actual PID. 2. Disconnect linkage to distinguish mechanical vane bind from electrical sensor wear. 3. Replace VGT actuator or clean vanes.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Fuel Injector Calibration Not Learned — ECU Reset/Swap
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest (SID208); after injector replacement or battery drain
symptoms: Rattling diesel knock on light throttle, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform Injector Pilot Injection Learn routine via diagnostic tool. 2. Verify coolant temp >70°C and zero active DTCs before running learn. 3. Test drive at steady cruise.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Hard Hot-Start Only (Cranks Long When Engine Hot)
phContext: Older Mitsubishi 4D56 / Toyota 2KD; internal HP pump/injector wear
symptoms: Starts instantly cold, cranks 8–10 seconds when hot
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor rail pressure during hot crank (must reach >20–25 MPa within 2 sec). 2. Pour cool water on HP pump head; if it starts immediately, pump plunger is worn. 3. Perform injector leak-off test.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Excessive White/Blue Smoke at Morning Cold Start
phContext: High-mileage L300, HiAce, Crosswind; worn valve stem seals or glow plugs
symptoms: Pungent white/blue smoke for 1–2 min, clears when warm
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test all glow plugs with clamp ammeter (expect ~12–18A per plug initially). 2. Check injector spray pattern/dribble. 3. Perform compression test if smoke persists warm.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Black Smoke Under Light Acceleration — Dirty Air Filter / EGR
phContext: Urban UV Express vans & delivery trucks; neglected air filter
symptoms: Thick black soot on takeoff, poor fuel economy
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect air filter restriction indicator and element. 2. Check EGR valve for incomplete closing. 3. Check injector over-fueling / boost leak.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Sudden Engine Runaway Risk — Turbo Oil Seal Failure
phContext: High-mileage turbo diesels; blown compressor oil seal filling intercooler
symptoms: Engine revs uncontrollably on its own oil, thick blue-white smoke
diagnosticSteps: 1. DO NOT run engine; inspect lower intercooler hose for pooled engine oil. 2. Check turbo shaft radial/axial play. 3. Drain intercooler and rebuild turbocharger.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Turbo Boost Control Solenoid Open — Broken Wire
phContext: Isuzu 4JJ1, Nissan Navara; brittle harness above turbo heat
symptoms: No boost, sluggish acceleration, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure boost solenoid coil resistance (15–35 ohms). 2. Test 12V ignition feed with test light. 3. Repair heat-hardened wiring pigtail.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: MAP/Boost Sensor Circuit Low — Shorted 5V or Ground
phContext: Toyota D-4D, Mitsubishi; pinched harness under intercooler
symptoms: No turbo boost, limp mode, MAP reads <15 kPa
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 5V reference at MAP plug. 2. Unplug sensor; if 5V returns, sensor is shorted internally. 3. Inspect harness under intercooler bracket.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: CKP Sensor Range/Performance — Metallic Debris on Tip
phContext: Manual transmission diesels with worn clutch/flywheel
symptoms: Intermittent bucking, tach needle drops, hard start
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove CKP sensor and inspect magnetic tip for clutch/ring-gear filings. 2. Scope CKP AC/Hall waveform for missing tooth distortion. 3. Clean tip and check air gap.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Brake Switch A/B Correlation — Dual Switch Misaligned
phContext: Ford Ranger, Toyota Hilux, Montero; worn pedal stopper pad
symptoms: Cruise control disabled, sudden power cut when braking/accelerating
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor Brake Switch 1 & 2 PIDs (must toggle simultaneously in opposite/same logic). 2. Inspect plastic pedal stopper pad. 3. Adjust or replace brake light switch.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control — Water in ECM
phContext: Flooded pickups/vans; moisture inside ECU case
symptoms: Random multi-injector shutoff, stalls in rain
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove ECM and inspect connector pins and PCB for corrosion. 2. Check injector harness for short to ground. 3. Clean/dry or replace ECM.

domainName: Common Rail Diesel (CRDi / D-4D / VGT / EGR / DPF)
title: DPF Regeneration Frequency — Fuel Dilution / Short Trips
phContext: Euro-4+ pickups used purely for short urban errands
symptoms: Frequent regen warnings, oil level rising above F mark
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check oil dipstick for thin diesel-diluted oil (change immediately if high). 2. Inspect injectors for over-fueling. 3. Advise highway drive cycle or forced regen.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Alternator Undercharging at Idle — Worn Carbon Brushes
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova, Mitsubishi; 80,000+ km city taxis/TNVS
symptoms: Battery light flickers at idle with A/C on, dead battery after traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure battery voltage at idle with headlights + A/C ON (spec >= 13.2V). 2. Check alternator B+ vs. battery + for voltage drop (<0.3V). 3. Replace worn brushes/regulator.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: System Voltage High (>15.5V) — Failed Voltage Regulator
phContext: Nissan, Mitsubishi, Hyundai; overcharging boiling battery acid
symptoms: Rotten-egg smell, swollen battery case, blown headlight bulbs
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure charging voltage at 2000 RPM (if >15.0V, regulator failed). 2. Check alternator sense (S) wire fuse/continuity (open S wire causes max output). 3. Replace regulator/alternator.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Battery Sulfation / Premature Death (12–18 Months)
phContext: Metro Manila daily commuters; high underhood heat + short trips
symptoms: Slow cranking after overnight park, resting voltage <12.2V
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform conductance/load test (CCA must be >70% rated; cranking >9.6V). 2. Check electrolyte specific gravity (if serviceable). 3. Verify charging voltage (13.8–14.4V).

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Parasitic Battery Drain — Aftermarket Dashcam / Tracker
phContext: TNVS/Grab & private cars; hardwired dashcam or GPS tracker stuck ON
symptoms: Battery dead after 2– 3 days parked, normal alternator test
diagnosticSteps: 1. Lock car, wait 30 min for CAN sleep, and measure milliamp draw in series (spec <30–50 mA). 2. Pull fuses one by one or measure mV drop across mini-fuses. 3. Rewire accessory to ACC/IG1.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Alternator Overheating & Diode Ripple — Blown Rectifier
phContext: SUVs with dual-fan A/C + aftermarket audio amp
symptoms: Whining noise from alternator, erratic ECU/TCM sensor glitches
diagnosticSteps: 1. Set DMM to AC Volts across battery terminals at 2000 RPM (spec <0.05V AC / 50 mV). 2. Scope charging waveform for missing phase. 3. Replace rectifier diode pack.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Generator Control Circuit — Smart Charging LIN/PWM Fault
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest, Mazda, Honda ELD; broken LIN/ALT-C wire
symptoms: Battery light on despite 13.5V fallback charging
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 1-pin or 3-pin alternator control plug for broken wire near fan shroud. 2. Scope LIN/PWM duty cycle from ECM/BCM. 3. Check Battery Monitoring Sensor (BMS) at negative post.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Starter Solenoid Clicks Only (No Crank) — Worn Contacts
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner/Vios (Denso starter); worn copper plunger contacts
symptoms: Rapid single click at key turn, headlights dim slightly, starts after 5–10 tries
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 12V at starter S-terminal during crank (if 12V present, solenoid/starter fault). 2. Check battery-to-starter cable drop (<0.4V). 3. Replace Denso solenoid plunger & contacts.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Slow Crank When Engine Hot — High Starter Resistance
phContext: High-mileage vans/pickups; heat-soaked starter armature or bad engine ground
symptoms: Cranks fast cold, drags slowly after highway run
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage drop between battery negative and engine block during crank (<0.3V). 2. Check starter current draw with clamp meter (120– 220A normal; >300A = shorted windings). 3. Clean ground straps or rebuild starter.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Corroded Battery Terminals — Acid Vapor Sulfation
phContext: All PH wet-cell batteries in humid climate; white/green crust on posts
symptoms: Sudden total power loss on key turn, dash blacks out
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage directly on lead battery posts vs. cable clamps during load. 2. Clean posts/clamps with baking soda solution and wire brush. 3. Apply terminal protector.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Alternator Belt Slippage — Cracked Serpentine Belt / Tensioner
phContext: Vehicles exposed to splash/flood; squealing belt under A/C load
symptoms: Loud screech on startup or A/C clutch engagement, voltage drops to 12.0V
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect belt ribs for glazing or cracks. 2. Check automatic tensioner travel and alternator decoupler pulley (OAP) freewheel. 3. Replace belt and seized OAP.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: False No-Comm / Low Voltage Reset — Loose Main Ground
phContext: Vehicles after transmission/clutch job; forgotten G101 engine ground
symptoms: Random stall over bumps, all dash lights reset
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect braided ground strap from cylinder head/transmission to chassis. 2. Perform voltage drop test under crank/load. 3. Scrape paint and torque ground bolt.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Blown Main Fusible Link (100A–140A) — Jump-Start Reversal
phContext: Roadside jump-start mistake; reversed jumper cables
symptoms: Complete dead vehicle (no horn, no hazards, no dash)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test continuity across main ALT/Battery fusible link block on positive terminal. 2. Check alternator diodes for dead short before replacing link. 3. Scan all ECUs for voltage damage.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Ignition Switch Contact Burnout — High Blower Current
phContext: Older Toyota/Mitsubishi/Honda without blower relay mod
symptoms: Accessories/A/C cut out until key is wiggled, no-crank intermittently
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage drop across ignition switch IG1/IG2/ACC terminals under load (>0.5V = bad). 2. Inspect switch backplate for melted plastic. 3. Replace switch and add external relay for heavy loads.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Starter Relay Circuit Low — Shorted Control Wire
phContext: Aftermarket remote-start / alarm splice fault
symptoms: Starter won't engage, starter relay fuse blown
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect aftermarket alarm/immobilizer starter-kill splice under dash. 2. Test starter relay socket pins (30, 85, 86, 87). 3. Remove corroded T-taps and solder properly.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Battery Light On With Normal 14.1V — Aftermarket Alternator
phContext: Replacement non-OEM alternator with incompatible L-terminal driver
symptoms: Battery warning lamp stays dimly or brightly lit, charges fine
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify OEM vs. aftermarket regulator internal circuit (lamp vs. ECM-controlled). 2. Check L-terminal voltage at KOEO and running. 3. Install OEM-spec regulator.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Intermittent No-Crank in P, Starts in N — Misaligned Inhibitor
phContext: Automatic cars (Vios, City, Innova); worn shifter bushing or moisture
symptoms: No crank in Park, starts immediately when shifted to Neutral
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Transmission Range Sensor (TRS) PID in Park vs. Neutral. 2. Inspect shifter cable bushing for play. 3. Clean/adjust neutral safety switch on transmission.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: System Voltage Malfunction — Corroded Engine Bay Fuse Box
phContext: Vehicles parked outdoors or washed with pressure washer
symptoms: Multiple random sensor DTCs, flickering cluster
diagnosticSteps: 1. Lift engine bay PDC/fuse box and inspect underside connectors for green corrosion. 2. Check main B+ stud torque. 3. Clean contacts with contact cleaner.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Alternator Clutch Pulley (OAP) Seized — Belt Chirp & Vibration
phContext: Modern diesels & sedans (Hilux, Ranger, Xpander, City)
symptoms: Rattling belt tensioner at idle, chirping on engine shutdown
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove belt and spin alternator pulley; must lock one way and freewheel the other. 2. If locked solid both ways, replace OAP with special spline tool. 3. Inspect belt.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Battery Voltage Low (Ford/Mazda) — Failed BMS Reset
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest/EcoSport; battery replaced without BMS reset
symptoms: Auto Start-Stop disabled, battery light/charging erratic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Load-test new battery. 2. Perform BMS Reset procedure via scan tool (or flash high-beam/brake sequence). 3. Verify target charging voltage stabilizes.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Starter Keeps Spinning After Key Release — Stuck Relay/Switch
phContext: Damaged ignition switch return spring or welded starter relay
symptoms: Loud grinding noise after engine fires, starter overheats
diagnosticSteps: 1. Immediately pull starter relay or disconnect battery. 2. Test if 12V remains on S-terminal with key in ON. 3. Replace welded relay or faulty ignition switch.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Parasitic Draw from Stuck Trunk / Glovebox Light
phContext: Sedans with bent trunk latch or broken pin switch
symptoms: Battery dead every morning, no obvious accessory left on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Fold rear seats or use phone camera to check if trunk light stays on when closed. 2. Measure current drop when pulling interior dome/trunk fuse. 3. Adjust or replace switch.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Weak Cranking Despite New Battery — High-Resistance Cable
phContext: Older SUVs/vans; internal green corrosion inside positive battery lug
symptoms: Battery tests 12.6V, drops to 6V at starter during crank
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage drop from battery (+) post to starter B+ stud while cranking (spec <0.4V). 2. Feel battery terminal/lug for extreme heat after cranking. 3. Replace corroded battery cable.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit — Broken ECM Sense
phContext: Honda/Chrysler/Ford; open field control wire
symptoms: Alternator stops charging completely, battery light on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check continuity of F-terminal wire from alternator to ECM. 2. Scope ECM field PWM command. 3. Replace alternator if field rotor is open (spec 2– 5 ohms across slip rings).

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Fuse Box Melted Slot (A/C or Fan Fuse) — Loose Blade Grip
phContext: High-mileage taxis/vans; loose fuse terminal causing resistance heat
symptoms: Cooling fan or A/C stops intermittently, plastic fuse melted
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect fuse socket female terminals for spread blades and heat discoloration. 2. Depin and replace terminal or bypass with external inline Maxi-fuse holder. 3. Check fan motor amperage draw.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Starter Bendix Spins Without Engaging Flywheel — Worn Clutch
phContext: High-mileage commuters; worn starter one-way overrunning clutch
symptoms: High-pitched whirring sound on key turn, engine doesn't crank
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect starter pinion teeth and flywheel ring gear teeth for damage. 2. Bench-test starter solenoid throw and pinion lock. 3. Replace starter drive/bendix assembly.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: ABS/TCS Lights On After Jump-Start — Low Voltage Latch
phContext: Modern CAN vehicles cranked with dying battery (<9.5V)
symptoms: Engine starts but ABS/VSC/EPS lights stay on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify charging voltage is steady 13.8–14.4V. 2. Scan all modules; clear low-voltage U-codes and C-codes. 3. Perform steering angle sensor zero-point calibration if needed.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Dash Flickers & Radio Resets on Hard Braking — Loose Ground
phContext: Vehicles with loose battery tie-down or under-tightened negative clamp
symptoms: Cluster blacks out momentarily during bumps or braking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Physically twist battery clamps (must not move). 2. Inspect battery hold-down bracket (preventing terminal contact with hood!). 3. Tighten clamps and clean posts.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Aftermarket Sound System Voltage Drop — Undersized Wiring
phContext: Modified hatchbacks/sedans; 1000W+ amp wired to stock 70A alternator
symptoms: Headlights dim with bass hits, battery dies in traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform Big-3 ground/charge cable upgrade (4 AWG). 2. Measure total amperage draw at idle with audio + A/C. 3. Upgrade alternator output or add AGM auxiliary battery.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: System Voltage Unstable — Loose Alternator B+ Nut
phContext: Vehicles recently serviced for timing belt or alternator
symptoms: Flickering headlights, erratic idle, intermittent battery warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check torque on alternator B+ output nut (often finger-loose causing arcing). 2. Inspect ring terminal for heat charring. 3. Clean and torque securely.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: 24V Dual-Battery Imbalance (12V Tap Draw)
phContext: 24V trucks/SUVs with 12V radio/dashcam tapped off ONE battery
symptoms: One battery always dead/boiling, other overcharged
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure resting voltage of Battery A vs. Battery B (must be within 0.1V). 2. Inspect for illegal 12V tap on center post. 3. Install proper 24V-to-12V DC-DC step-down converter.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: 12V Accessory Socket Dead — Coin Dropped in Socket
phContext: Family MPVs (Xpander, Avanza, Innova); metallic coin shorting socket
symptoms: Dashcam/phone charger dead, blown 15A ACC/CIG fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect inside of 12V socket with flashlight for coins or foil. 2. Replace blown 15A ACC/CIG fuse in cabin fuse box. 3. Test socket 12V with DMM.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Open — Relay Failure
phContext: Diesel/Gas ECMs; blown Actuator/ETC relay
symptoms: Multiple actuator DTCs simultaneously (EGR, VGT, throttle)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ECM/Actuator main relay and associated 15A/20A fuse. 2. Measure 12V at affected actuator connectors. 3. Trace harness for short to ground.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Keyless Push-Start Won't Crank — Weak Brake Switch
phContext: Push-button start vehicles (Vios G, Xpander, City RS)
symptoms: Accessory turns ON, pressing Start does not crank, brake lights stay off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if brake lights illuminate when pressing pedal. 2. Inspect brake light fuse and 4-pin brake switch. 3. Check Start-Stop button status PID in BCM.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Parasitic Draw from Stuck Radiator Fan Relay
phContext: Older sedans/SUVs; welded fan relay contacts keeping fan on key-off
symptoms: Radiator fan runs until battery dies overnight
diagnosticSteps: 1. Feel fan relay for warmth with key off. 2. Pull fan relay; if fan stops, replace welded relay. 3. Check ECT sensor if ECM is commanding fan ON.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Battery Boiling / Acid Spill in Tray — Overcharging
phContext: Older alternator with mechanical/failed IC regulator (>15.5V)
symptoms: Acid corrosion eating fender/tray, strong sulfur odor
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage at 2500 RPM (>15.0V = replace regulator). 2. Neutralize acid in battery tray with baking soda + water. 3. Replace heat-damaged battery.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: ECM/PCM Power Relay De-Energized Too Early
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Kia; weak battery or loose relay pin
symptoms: MIL on after cold start, momentary memory loss
diagnosticSteps: 1. Load-test battery (voltage sag at shutdown triggers P068A). 2. Replace main relay if contacts chatter. 3. Inspect ECM keep-alive memory (KAM) fuse.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Alternator No-Charge After Engine Wash — Wet Slip Rings
phContext: Vehicles washed with high-pressure water directly on alternator
symptoms: Battery light on immediately after car wash
diagnosticSteps: 1. Blow out alternator vents with compressed air and let dry. 2. Check excitation/IG fuse if shorted while wet. 3. Test voltage output once dry.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Dim Headlights at Idle, Bright When Revving
phContext: Older vehicles with weak battery + undersized/worn alternator
symptoms: Lights dim noticeably at stoplights
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check idle charging voltage with lights + A/C on. 2. Check alternator belt tension. 3. Load-test battery and check alternator stator phase output.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Invalid Data from ABS — Low Voltage During Crank
phContext: Modern Toyotas/Hondas/Mitsubish is with aging 12V battery
symptoms: ABS/VSC warning flashes briefly during cranking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test battery CCA and cranking voltage (replace if <9.6V). 2. Clear historical U-codes. 3. Verify alternator output.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Starter Drain / High Amperage — Dragging Bushings
phContext: High-mileage diesel starters (HiAce, L300, Hilux)
symptoms: Battery drains fast on crank, cables get hot
diagnosticSteps: 1. Clamp-test starter draw (>350A on 12V diesel indicates worn bushings/armature drag). 2. Bench-disassemble starter, inspect commutator and brushes. 3. Replace bushings/armature.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Relay Clicking Rapidly (Machine-Gun Sound) on Crank
phContext: Discharged battery (10.5– 11.8V) or poor terminal contact
symptoms: Rapid relay chatter, dash lights blink wildly
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure battery resting voltage (<12.0V = discharged). 2. Jump-start or charge battery and load-test. 3. Check alternator charging once started.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Cruise Control Multi-Function Input — Clock Spring / Voltage
phContext: Pickups/SUVs on NLEX/SCTEX; corroded steering wheel switches
symptoms: Cruise control drops out or refuses to set
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read cruise switch PIDs while pressing SET/RES/CANCEL. 2. Check clock spring continuity. 3. Check brake/clutch switch correlation.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Horn Works Only When Steering Turned — Broken Clock Spring
phContext: High-mileage city taxis/MPVs; worn spiral cable ribbon
symptoms: Horn dead straight-ahead, works at 90-degree turn; SRS light may follow
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test horn relay by jumping terminal 30 to 87 (verifies horn & fuse). 2. Measure continuity across clock spring horn circuit while turning wheel. 3. Replace clock spring.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Power Window Slow / Stops Halfway — Dry Run Channel + Drop
phContext: Older Vios/City/Civic; dusty rubber tracks + weak motor
symptoms: Window struggles in rain, blows thermal breaker
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure voltage at window motor connector under load (check door jamb boot for broken wire). 2. Lubricate rubber window channels with silicone spray. 3. Inspect motor brushes.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Headlight Connector Melted — Over-Wattage Halogen Bulbs
phContext: Drivers upgrading 55W H4 bulbs to 100W/90W without relay harness
symptoms: One headlight out, melted 3-pin H4 plug
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect H4 socket for melted plastic. 2. Install ceramic H4 sockets and dedicated dual-relay harness directly from battery. 3. Revert to 55W/60W or compliant LED.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Intermittent Fuel Gauge Drop to Empty — Sulfated Sender
phContext: PH vehicles running high-sulfur/ethanol fuel blends
symptoms: Fuel needle drops to E with warning light, then recovers
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Fuel Level Sensor voltage/ohm PID. 2. Measure sender resistance sweep (typically 10–300 ohms) outside tank. 3. Clean silver-palladium wiper or replace sender.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Brake Lights Stay Stuck ON — Broken Plastic Pedal Stopper
phContext: Toyota, Honda, Nissan, Mitsubishi; brittle 10-year-old plastic pad
symptoms: Brake lights stay on overnight draining battery, shifter stuck in Park
diagnosticSteps: 1. Look on driver floor mat for shattered white/blue plastic fragments. 2. Inspect brake pedal arm hole where switch plunger rests. 3. Snap in new rubber/nylon stopper pad.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Radiator Fan Fuse Blows Repeatedly — Seized Fan Motor
phContext: Traffic-heavy cars; worn cooling fan motor bearings drawing >35A
symptoms: Engine overheats in traffic, 30A/40A fan fuse blown
diagnosticSteps: 1. Spin fan blade by hand (must spin freely without grind). 2. Measure fan running amperage with clamp meter (normal 10–18A; >25A = failing motor). 3. Replace fan motor.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Internal Control Module KAM Error — Disconnected Battery
phContext: Vehicles with frequent battery disconnects or corroded backup fuse
symptoms: Stored code after battery change, learned idle/fuel trims lost
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Backup/DOME/KAM 10A fuse in engine bay. 2. Verify constant 12V (KL30) at ECM pin with key off. 3. Clear code and run idle relearn.

domainName: Charging, Starting & 12V/24V Power Distribution
title: Total Electrical Blackout Over Pothole — Loose Ground Bolt
phContext: Vehicles after body/fender repair; unpainted/loose chassis ground
symptoms: Car dies completely over lubak, restarts when wiggled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect battery negative cable to fender apron and chassis rail. 2. Check main fuse box B+ bolt. 3. Clean paint under ground lug and torque tightly.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Engine Hydrolock After Flood — Water in Cylinders
phContext: Low-clearance sedans (Vios, City, Mirage) stalled in >30 cm floodwater
symptoms: Starter clunks/locks solid, engine won't turn over
diagnosticSteps: 1. DO NOT force starter! Remove all spark plugs (or glow plugs/injectors on diesel). 2. Crank engine to expel water from cylinders. 3. Check engine oil for milky emulsion and inspect air filter for saturation; check rod straightness.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Lost Comm with BCM — Flooded Floorpan Kick-Panel
phContext: Toyota, Mitsubishi, Honda; floodwater reaching cabin sill/kick-panel
symptoms: Power windows/locks dead, no-start, wipers running nonstop
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove driver/passenger kick panels and inspect BCM/junction block for water line and green verdigris. 2. Unplug all harness connectors, flush with contact cleaner, and dry. 3. Inspect PCB for corroded vias.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: SRS Airbag Module Internal Fault — Wet Under-Seat ECU
phContext: Sedans/MPVs with SRS module bolted to center floor tunnel
symptoms: SRS airbag light solid after cabin flooding
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect center console floor tunnel for damp carpet/silt. 2. Remove SRS ECU (battery disconnected 10+ min!) and check pins for corrosion. 3. Replace SRS module if PCB is water-damaged.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Lost Comm with TCM — Submerged Transmission Connector
phContext: Automatic/CVT cars driven through deep flood; underbody TCM/range plug
symptoms: Gear indicator dashes (---), stuck in 3rd gear limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect transmission main round/rectangular connector and range switch for water. 2. Check transmission breather tube for water entry (check ATF/CVTF for pink milkshake!). 3. Dry connector and flush fluid.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Milky Engine Oil — Floodwater Entry via Dipstick/Breather
phContext: Any vehicle parked in waist-deep floodwater
symptoms: Creamy beige sludge on dipstick and oil filler cap
diagnosticSteps: 1. Do not start engine until oil is drained. 2. Drain oil pan, replace oil filter, refill with cheap flush oil, run 5 min, and drain again. 3. Check transmission and differential fluids for water too.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Milky ATF / CVT Fluid — Submerged Gearbox Breather
phContext: Vios, Mirage, Xpander, City; floodwater sucked in as hot gearbox cools
symptoms: Transmission shudders, slips, then fails completely
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pull ATF dipstick/check plug; milky pink fluid = water contamination. 2. Perform full machine/pan-drop fluid exchange (3x drain-and-fill minimum) and replace filter. 3. Relocate breather hose higher if possible.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Delayed ECU Failure (2–8 Weeks Post-Flood) — Pin Corrosion
phContext: Used/flooded cars cleaned up without opening under-dash/floor plugs
symptoms: Intermittent stall, phantom DTCs appearing weeks after typhoon
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect under-carpet splice packs (green/white powder = galvanic corrosion). 2. Pull ECM/PCM connectors and look for blue-green pin oxidation. 3. Re-pin damaged terminals and seal with dielectric grease.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Short — Flood Silt in Tone Ring
phContext: All ABS-equipped vehicles after driving through muddy floodwater
symptoms: ABS/VSC lights on, false ABS activation at low speed
