diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect wheel hub tone rings and magnetic encoders for packed mud/rust. 2. Clean sensor face and tone ring with brake cleaner. 3. Check sensor connector under fender liner for water.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Seized Alternator Bearings — Floodwater Immersion
phContext: Low-mounted alternators (Mirage, Vios, Accent) after flood crossing
symptoms: Loud grinding whine from belt area, belt snaps, no charge
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove serpentine belt and spin alternator pulley by hand (rough/locked = ruined bearings). 2. Disassemble alternator, replace front/rear bearings, and clean rotor/stator mud. 3. Check starter and A/C compressor pulley bearings too.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: A/C Compressor Clutch Bearing Seized — Flood Silt
phContext: Low-mounted A/C compressors; floodwater washing grease out of pulley
symptoms: Loud howling noise even with A/C OFF, smoke from belt
diagnosticSteps: 1. Spin A/C pulley with belt off; check for play or roughness. 2. Inspect clutch coil resistance (3–4 ohms) for water short. 3. Replace pulley bearing and clutch coil.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Electric Power Steering (EPS) Rack Water Ingress
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis, Honda City/Civic, Mitsubishi Mirage (rack-mounted EPS)
symptoms: Heavy steering, EPS warning light, grinding noise when turning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect EPS rack rubber bellows/boots for tears letting floodwater in. 2. Scan EPS module for torque sensor or motor overcurrent DTCs. 3. Dry/rebuild rack motor or replace EPS rack.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: ECU/Module Internal Defect — Under-Seat Amplifier/ECU
phContext: SUVs/MPVs with under-seat power amp, 4WD ECU, or hybrid blower
symptoms: Audio dead, 4WD flashing, or parasitic drain after cabin flood
diagnosticSteps: 1. Lift front seats and inspect under-seat electronics for water stains. 2. Disconnect damaged module to check if CAN bus recovers. 3. Clean PCB with isopropyl alcohol or replace module.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Starter Motor Filled with Mud — No Crank Post-Flood
phContext: Pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Ranger, Montero) crossing muddy provincial floods
symptoms: Dead click at start, starter draws >400A and smokes
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove starter motor and open end-cap; flush out dried silt/rust. 2. Inspect brush holder springs (often rusted stuck) and commutator. 3. Clean, lubricate planetary gears, and bench-test.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Downstream/Upstream O2 Sensor Thermal Shock Failure
phContext: Hot exhaust submerged in cold floodwater
symptoms: Check Engine Light on immediately after flood crossing, O2 dead
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read B1S1/B1S2 live voltage (flatlined at 0.45V or 0V). 2. Check for water inside O2 connector plug (reference air vents through harness wires!). 3. Replace cracked ceramic O2 sensor.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Headlight / Taillight Ballast Short — Condensation
phContext: Modern LED/HID headlights (Xpander, Fortuner, City) with submerged vent
symptoms: One headlight dead, moisture droplets inside lens, blown fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove headlight assembly and inspect bottom-mounted LED/HID driver module for water. 2. Dry housing thoroughly and check butyl seal. 3. Replace shorted LED driver module.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Cabin Blower Motor Squealing / Dead — Flooded Footwell
phContext: Passenger footwell blower motors submerged during deep cabin flood
symptoms: A/C fan dead or squeals loudly, blows 30A/40A heater fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove blower motor under glovebox and drain trapped water. 2. Check blower resistor / PWM MOSFET module for corrosion. 3. Replace rusted blower motor.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Accelerator Pedal Sensor E Low — Floor Silt Corrosion
phContext: Drive-by-wire vehicles with floor-hinged or low-mounted APP
symptoms: Limp mode, vehicle won't rev above 1500 RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug pedal sensor and check for mud/green pins. 2. Measure APP1 and APP2 outputs with DMM. 3. Clean pins or replace pedal assembly.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Rear Drum Brakes Seized / Rusted to Shoes Post-Flood
phContext: Sedans/pickups parked for 2 days after driving through flood
symptoms: Car refuses to roll in Drive/Reverse, loud bang when freeing
diagnosticSteps: 1. Jack rear wheels and remove brake drums. 2. Clean rust, mud, and glazed brake dust; lubricate backing plate contact points. 3. Inspect wheel cylinders for torn boots.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Clutch Disc Rusted to Flywheel — Manual Cars Post-Flood
phContext: Manual Vios, Mirage, L300, Hilux parked wet after flood
symptoms: Engine starts in neutral, impossible to shift into any gear running
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect slave cylinder travel first. 2. If hydraulics work, disc is seized to flywheel; safely break free or pull transmission. 3. Replace rusted clutch kit and pilot bearing.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Engine Control System Malfunction Flag in ABS — Flooded Sensor
phContext: Toyota/Lexus vehicles; any engine MIL triggers VSC/TRAC lights
symptoms: ABS + VSC + Check Engine lights all on together after rain
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan Engine ECM first (C1201 is a secondary flag, not an ABS defect). 2. Fix primary engine/O2/MAF water fault. 3. Clear codes in both ECM and ABS.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Fuel Tank Water Contamination — Submerged Vent/Cap
phContext: Vehicles sitting in deep floodwater; water enters EVAP vent or cap
symptoms: Engine sputters and dies 10 minutes after flood, restarts briefly
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect fuel line at rail and pump sample into clear jar (water sinks to bottom). 2. Drop/drain fuel tank completely and dry. 3. Replace fuel filter and flush injectors.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Control Module Comm Bus A Off — Wet Under-Carpet Splice
phContext: Vehicles with CAN bus junction connector under driver carpet
symptoms: All warning lights on, tach/speedo drop to zero, no crank
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure CAN-H to CAN-L resistance (normal 60 ohms; <40 or >120 ohms = fault). 2. Measure CAN-H/L voltage to ground (2.6V / 2.4V). 3. Lift carpet to dry flooded CAN star connector.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Differential / Transfer Case Milky Oil — Submerged Breather
phContext: 4x4 Pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Ranger, Montero, D-Max) fording rivers/floods
symptoms: Whining rear differential noise weeks after flood crossing
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove rear differential fill plug and check oil color (gray/milky = water). 2. Drain and refill with GL-5 gear oil; repeat after 500 km if needed. 3. Extend breather hose into engine bay.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Immobilizer / Key Transponder Not Detected — Wet Antenna
phContext: Cars with flooded steering column/ignition switch area
symptoms: Security light flashes fast, engine cranks 1 sec and dies (or no crank)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check immobilizer coil ring around key cylinder for moisture. 2. Verify 12V/GND/DATA at immobilizer amplifier. 3. Dry BCM and re-sync keys if memory corrupted.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Radiator Cooling Fan Motor Dead — Submerged Mud
phContext: Low-clearance cars; mud jamming fan motor brushes
symptoms: Overheating in traffic after flood, blown 30A fan fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test fan motor directly with fused 12V jumper. 2. Disassemble fan motor or replace if commutator is silt-packed. 3. Flush radiator fins of dried mud!

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Overheating Due to Mud-Clogged Radiator/Condenser Fins
phContext: 4x4s and cars after muddy typhoon floods (e.g., Ulysses/Carina silt)
symptoms: Engine temp climbs on highway/hills despite working fan
diagnosticSteps: 1. Shine flashlight through radiator from engine side; blocked light = mud cake. 2. Remove grille/fan shroud and gently flush fins from back to front with low-pressure hose. 3. Do NOT bend fins with pressure washer.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Underbody Fuel Pump Module Rusted/Shorted — Flood Silt
phContext: MPVs/pickups with external frame-rail pump or low tank access
symptoms: Car dies weeks after flood, blown fuel pump fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect top of fuel pump hat for rusted terminals and wet silt. 2. Measure pump resistance and current draw. 3. Replace pump pigtail and fuel pump assembly.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Horn Sounds Continuously or Dead — Flooded Bumper Horns
phContext: Horns mounted low behind front bumper grille
symptoms: Horn blasts nonstop in the middle of the night or goes silent
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug horns behind bumper and drain water from spiral snail shells. 2. Check horn relay for welded contacts. 3. Replace waterlogged horns pointing downward.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Parking Sensors / Rear Camera Dead — Mud & Water Ingress
phContext: SUVs/MPVs with bumper-mounted sonar sensors & reverse camera
symptoms: Continuous false beep in Reverse, black/fuzzy backup screen
diagnosticSteps: 1. Listen/feel each sonar sensor in Reverse (working sensors tick faintly). 2. Unplug rear bumper harness and check for green corrosion. 3. Dry camera connector and seal.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Transmission Range Sensor (PRNDL) Fault — Flooded Switch
phContext: Automatic cars after deep puddle crossing; switch on side of gearbox
symptoms: No crank in Park, reverse lights stay on, wrong gear shown on dash
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor TR/Inhibitor switch PIDs on scan tool while moving shifter. 2. Remove switch from gearbox side, open/clean oxidized copper contacts, or replace. 3. Realign switch index marks.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Door Lock Actuators Cycling Randomly — Wet Door Harness
phContext: Flooded cars with water inside door panels or A-pillar boots
symptoms: Doors lock/unlock by themselves, draining battery
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect rubber bellows between door and A-pillar; inspect multi-pin plug for green corrosion. 2. Check door ajar switches for water shorts. 3. Clean pins and dry door lock actuator.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Power Seat / Lumbar Stuck or Smoking — Submerged Motors
phContext: SUVs/sedans with electric seats after cabin flooding
symptoms: Power seat won't move, blows 30A power seat fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug seat harness under seat and check for water line. 2. Test each seat motor independently with fused jumper. 3. Clean switch contacts and dry floor harness.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Alternator Rotor/Stator Shorted — Salt/Brackish Floodwater
phContext: Coastal areas (Navotas, Malabon, Bacoor, Cavite) tidal flooding
symptoms: Severe green/white salt crust on alternator, instant dead battery
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect alternator casing for white salt bloom. 2. Test stator-to-ground insulation. 3. Replace alternator and flush engine bay with fresh water + anti-corrosion spray.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Smart Key / Push-Start Antenna Error — Wet Center Console
phContext: Push-start cars with floodwater reaching center console tunnel
symptoms: Key Not Detected on dash, must touch fob to start button
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove center console trim and inspect interior LF key antenna plug. 2. Check for water inside shift-lock/console harness. 3. Replace corroded LF antenna.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Wiper Motor Runs Slowly or Stops — Flooded Cowl Drain
phContext: Cars parked under trees during typhoons; clogged cowl leaf drains
symptoms: Water overflows cowl into wiper motor & cabin air intake
diagnosticSteps: 1. Clear leaves/mud from windshield cowl drains. 2. Inspect wiper motor park switch contacts for water corrosion. 3. Dry cabin filter box.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: EPS Torque Sensor Calibration Lost — Flooded Column/Rack
phContext: Toyota/Suzuki/Hyundai EPS after flood battery disconnect
symptoms: EPS light on, steering pulls to one side
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check EPS module for water damage first. 2. Perform Torque Sensor Zero-Point Calibration on level ground with wheels straight. 3. Verify steering angle PID reads 0°.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Rear Wheel Bearings Roaring — Floodwater Washout
phContext: Sedans/MPVs driven through deep floods; grease washed out of hubs
symptoms: Loud humming/growling noise increasing with speed (40+ km/h)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Lift wheels, spin by hand while holding coil spring to feel vibration. 2. Check for hub play. 3. Replace noisy wheel bearing/hub assembly (and ABS sensor if integrated).

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: 4WD Transfer Case Actuator Stuck — Flooded Vent/Motor
phContext: 4x4 Pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Fortuner, Montero, Ranger)
symptoms: 4WD light flashing, refuses to engage 4H/4L
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect transfer case shift motor connector under chassis for mud/water. 2. Open actuator cap to check limit switch contacts for rust. 3. Clean contacts and seal O-ring.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Fog Lamps Filled with Water — Cracked Lens / Missing Cap
phContext: Low bumper fog lights submerged in urban puddles
symptoms: Fog light bulbs blow repeatedly, brown water inside lens
diagnosticSteps: 1. Drain lamp housing and inspect rear bulb O-ring seal. 2. Check bumper fog light relay and ground. 3. Replace cracked lamp assembly.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: EVAP Small Leak — Rusted Fuel Filler Neck / Tank Top
phContext: Coastal PH vehicles exposed to brackish floodwater
symptoms: MIL on, fuel smell near rear wheel arch
diagnosticSteps: 1. Smoke-test EVAP system and inspect steel filler neck behind wheel liner for pinholes. 2. Inspect top of fuel tank lock ring. 3. Replace corroded filler neck.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Instrument Cluster Gauges Dead / Dim — Moisture in PCB
phContext: Cars with flooded dash or extreme cabin humidity/mold
symptoms: Speedometer/tacho meter dead or segments missing, mold smell
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove cluster and inspect rear connectors for green corrosion. 2. Inspect cluster PCB with magnifier for corroded SMD resistors/traces. 3. Ultrasonic clean PCB and reflow joints.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Tailgate / Trunk Latch Won't Open — Water in Microswitch
phContext: Hatchbacks/SUVs (Wigo, Mirage, Xpander, Fortuner) in heavy rain
symptoms: Push-button trunk release unresponsive
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove tailgate trim and unplug rubber-booted release switch. 2. Check 12V/ground/signal at switch and test latch actuator directly. 3. Replace waterlogged trunk switch.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Clutch Slave Cylinder Seized / Leak — Muddy Bellhousing
phContext: Manual pickups/vans after muddy flood crossing
symptoms: Clutch pedal drops to floor or feels spongy
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect external slave cylinder boot for mud tear and fluid leak. 2. Bleed hydraulic system; if fluid is black/rusty, rebuild master & slave cylinders. 3. Check clutch fork pivot.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Airbag Clock Spring / Impact Sensor Corrosion — Front Bumper
phContext: Cars hitting floodwater wave; front crash sensor behind grille
symptoms: SRS light on with front crash sensor DTC (B0090–B0095)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect battery 10 min before touching SRS. 2. Inspect front impact sensor plug behind radiator support for green pins. 3. Replace corroded sensor/pigtail.

domainName: Flood / Water-Ingress & Corrosion Electrical Faults (PH Typhoon Context)
title: Persistent Mold & Electrical Gremlins — Wet Carpet Jute
phContext: Flooded cars dried only on surface without pulling seats/carpet
symptoms: Foggy windows, musty odor, recurring floor harness faults
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove seats, center console, and carpet completely; discard soaked jute padding. 2. Wash floorpan, dry harness splices with heat gun, and apply anti-corrosion spray. 3. Reassemble only when bone-dry.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Overheating ONLY When A/C is ON in Traffic
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova, Honda City, Mitsubishi; weak condenser/radiator fan
symptoms: Temp gauge climbs past 3/4 in traffic with A/C on, drops when A/C off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify BOTH radiator and condenser fans run at high speed when A/C compressor engages. 2. Check fan motor RPM/amp draw (weak brushes spin slowly). 3. Clean gap between condenser and radiator of leaves/dust.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Blows Warm Air at Idle, Cold When Driving Fast
phContext: Sedans/MPVs in heavy traffic; high head pressure from poor condenser cooling
symptoms: Cool on NLEX/SLEX, hot at stoplights
diagnosticSteps: 1. Hook up manifold gauges: check high-side pressure at idle (>250–300 psi = poor condenser airflow or overcharge). 2. Check condenser fan operation and fins. 3. Spray water on condenser; if temp drops, fix airflow.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit — Burned Relay / ECM Driver
phContext: Honda City/Civic, Ford, Hyundai; high fan current burning relay
symptoms: Engine overheats at idle, fan never turns on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Command Fan 1 ON via scan tool. 2. Check 30A/40A fan fuse and swap fan relay. 3. Jump fan motor directly; if it spins, trace relay control wire to ECM.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Cooling Fan 2 Control Circuit — High-Speed Fan Failure
phContext: Dual-speed fan systems (Ford, Hyundai, Honda); failed fan resistor
symptoms: Low speed works, high speed never engages under A/C load
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect fan shroud resistor pack (often open thermal fuse). 2. Test Fan High relay and wiring. 3. Replace resistor or fan assembly.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Viscous Fan Clutch Weak — Diesel SUV Overheating on Hills
phContext: Toyota Fortuner/Hilux, Montero, Isuzu; silicone fluid leaked out
symptoms: Temp climbs on Tagaytay/Baguio climbs with A/C on
diagnosticSteps: 1. When engine is hot, shut off and spin fan blade by hand (should have firm resistance, not spin freely). 2. Check front of fan clutch for oily dust/silicone leak. 3. Replace viscous fan clutch.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor Low — Refrigerant Leak
phContext: All modern PH cars; leaking evaporator core or O-ring
symptoms: A/C compressor clutch never engages, warm air
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read A/C Pressure PID (if <30 psi, system is empty/leaking). 2. Check 5V/GND/Signal at pressure transducer. 3. Nitrogen/UV-dye leak test evaporator, condenser, and Schrader valves.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Pressure Sensor High — Overcharged or Blocked Drier
phContext: Cars serviced by roadside shops adding gas without gauges
symptoms: A/C cuts off every 10 seconds in heat, compressor knocks
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check A/C Pressure PID (>400 psi triggers safety cutout). 2. Connect manifold gauges to check static & running high-side pressure. 3. Recover, vacuum, and recharge exact OEM gram weight.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Compressor Clutch Slips When Hot — Excessive Air Gap
phContext: High-mileage Vios/Innova/City; worn clutch plate shim gap
symptoms: A/C cold for 15 min, then blows warm in traffic; clutch won't pull in
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure clutch hub air gap with feeler gauge (spec 0.35–0.65 mm; >0.8 mm slips hot). 2. Verify 12V reaches clutch coil when warm. 3. Remove thin shim washer or replace clutch assembly.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C ECV (Electronic Control Valve) Failure — Variable Compressor
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis/Fortuner (clutchless/ECV), Hyundai, Kia
symptoms: A/C takes 10+ minutes to cool or cools only at high RPM
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope/measure PWM duty cycle at compressor ECV connector. 2. Check low/high side gauge pressures (if both equalize around 100–120 psi at idle, ECV is stuck). 3. Replace ECV valve on compressor.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Radiator Plastic End-Tank Hairline Crack — Thermal Fatigue
phContext: 6+ year old sedans/MPVs; brittle plastic top tank near neck
symptoms: Sweet coolant smell, slow coolant loss, overheating after traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressurize cooling system to 100– 110 kPa (15 psi) with hand tester. 2. Inspect top plastic tank seam and hose necks for pink/green crust. 3. Replace radiator and cap.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Weak Radiator Cap Seal — Coolant Boiling in Overflow Tank
phContext: Vehicles using tap water instead of 50/50 coolant; rusted cap spring
symptoms: Overflow reservoir bubbles/overflows after shutdown, radiator low
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressure-test radiator cap (must hold 0.9–1.1 bar per cap rating). 2. Inspect rubber seal for swelling or rust. 3. Replace cap and flush rusty tap water with premixed OAT coolant.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Rusted Water Pump Impeller — Tap Water Corrosion
phContext: Older cars topped up with tap water instead of ethylene glycol coolant
symptoms: Overheats at both idle and highway, no visible leak, upper hose cool
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check radiator flow with cap off (cold-to-warm transition). 2. Feel temp difference between upper and lower radiator hoses. 3. Remove water pump to inspect eroded impeller blades.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Evaporator Frozen Solid — Bad Thermistor / Low Freon
phContext: SUVs/vans on long provincial trips; airflow stops from vents
symptoms: A/C cold for 1 hour, then air stops blowing despite fan roaring
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Evaporator Temp Sensor PID (stuck >5°C while evaporator is ice-cold = skewed thermistor). 2. Check low-side pressure (<20 psi causes freeze-up). 3. Replace evaporator thermistor or fix leak.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Clogged Cabin Air Filter — Weak Vent Airflow & Musty Odor
phContext: Metro Manila vehicles; diesel soot & dust clogging filter in 6 months
symptoms: Blower fan sounds loud, barely any air from vents, poor cooling
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pull cabin filter behind glovebox; check for black soot/leaves. 2. Inspect evaporator face with borescope for mold mat. 3. Replace filter and clean evaporator.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Amplifier / Relay Stuck ON — Drains Battery / Freezes Evap
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova; welded A/C magnetic clutch (MG CLT) relay
symptoms: A/C compressor stays engaged even with A/C button OFF
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pull MG CLT relay; if clutch disengages, replace welded relay. 2. If still engaged, check A/C amplifier output wire for short to ground. 3. Verify pressure switch.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Dual-Aircon Rear Blower Dead — Rear Relay / Resistor
phContext: Toyota Innova/HiAce, Mitsubishi Xpander/Montero, Suzuki Ertiga
symptoms: Front A/C cold, rear ceiling vents blow nothing or only High
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check rear blower fuse and relay in cabin box. 2. Test rear blower resistor block (thermal fuse open = High speed only). 3. Check rear motor brushes.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Coolant Leak at Plastic T-Fitting / Bypass Pipe
phContext: Toyota, Ford, Mazda; brittle plastic heater/bypass tees cracking
symptoms: Sudden rapid coolant loss and steam under hood
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressure-test system cold and trace wet spots behind cylinder head/intake. 2. Replace brittle plastic tees (upgrade to brass/aluminum if available). 3. Bleed air pockets thoroughly.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Thermostat Removed by Mechanic — Overcooling & High Fuel Use
phContext: Used cars bought in PH with thermostat removed to 'prevent overheat'
symptoms: Temp gauge stays at 1/4, poor mileage, sludge buildup
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor ECT PID (hovers 60–70°C instead of 85–92°C). 2. Remove thermostat housing to verify OEM thermostat is present. 3. Install proper OEM thermostat and bleed system.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: ECT Sensor Range/Performance — Air Pocket in Cooling System
phContext: Vehicles recently serviced for radiator/hose without proper bleeding
symptoms: Temp gauge spikes suddenly then drops, fan cycles erratically
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check coolant level in radiator (not just overflow tank) when cold. 2. Bleed air using spill-free funnel at highest point until thermostat opens twice. 3. Verify ECT rises smoothly.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Head Gasket Blown — Exhaust Gas in Coolant (Post-Overheat)
phContext: Cars driven after overheating in traffic; warped aluminum head
symptoms: Coolant blows out overflow bottle immediately on cold rev, misfire
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform combustion leak (block) test with blue chemical fluid at radiator neck. 2. Pressurize cylinders with leak-down tester while watching radiator for bubbles. 3. Machine cylinder head and replace gasket.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Black Death — A/C Compressor Seizure Contaminating Lines
phContext: High-mileage taxis/vans; neglected compressor oil/refrigerant
symptoms: Loud rattle, belt smokes/snaps when A/C turns on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Disconnect A/C line and inspect oil (gray/black metallic paste = Black Death). 2. Replace compressor, condenser (parallel-flow cannot be flushed), expansion valve, and drier. 3. Flush evaporator & hoses.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Drain Hose Clogged — Water Flooding Passenger Floor
phContext: Dusty/moldy cabin environments; slime plugging rubber drain tube
symptoms: Water sloshes behind dash on turns, passenger carpet soaked
diagnosticSteps: 1. Locate rubber A/C drain hose under passenger firewall/chassis. 2. Clear slime plug gently with compressed air or zip-tie. 3. Flush evaporator box.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Engine Oil Cooler / ATF Warmer Internal Leak — Milkshake
phContext: Cars with radiator-integrated ATF cooler or oil-to-water cooler
symptoms: Pink strawberry milkshake in radiator or ATF dipstick
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressure-test radiator ATF cooler port separately. 2. Inspect engine oil cooler gaskets/plate. 3. Replace cooler/radiator and flush BOTH engine/trans and cooling system.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit — Open Wire
phContext: Vehicles after front bumper repair; pinched sensor harness
symptoms: A/C compressor won't engage, radiator fan runs high nonstop
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 5V, GND, and signal at 3-pin A/C pressure sensor. 2. Read A/C pressure PID (0 psi or 500 psi indicates open/short). 3. Repair bumper harness.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: PWM Cooling Fan Controller Failure — Fan Runs Full or Zero
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest/Focus, Mazda, Hyundai; burnt PWM module on shroud
symptoms: Fan either stays off (overheats) or runs 100% draining battery
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check heavy 12V/GND at fan module and scope ECM PWM signal wire. 2. If PWM signal is valid but fan doesn't respond, module is faulty. 3. Replace fan control module.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Blend Door Actuator Clicking — Stripped Plastic Gear
phContext: Automatic climate control SUVs/sedans (Fortuner, Montero, City)
symptoms: Loud rhythmic ticking behind dashboard at key-on, wrong vent temp
diagnosticSteps: 1. Locate clicking actuator behind glovebox or driver footwell. 2. Scan HVAC module for blend/mode door DTCs. 3. Replace actuator and run HVAC calibration.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Clogged Radiator Core — Stop-Leak Sealant or Rust Scale
phContext: Used cars treated with 'stop-leak' powder/liquid
symptoms: Overheats on highway climbs; top of radiator hot, bottom stone-cold
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan radiator face with IR thermometer (cold patches = clogged tubes). 2. Flush or replace clogged radiator. 3. Never use stop-leak additives.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Turns Off Under Acceleration — WOT Cutout Stuck
phContext: Vehicles with faulty TPS or engine running hot (>108°C)
symptoms: A/C blows warm whenever accelerating lightly
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor A/C Cut-off reason PID in Engine ECM (ECT high, WOT, or high pressure). 2. Check ECT and TPS calibration. 3. Address overheating or high head pressure.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Heater Core Bypassed Incorrectly — Restricts Coolant Flow
phContext: PH tropical repairs where mechanic plugged heater hoses instead of looping
symptoms: Cylinder #4 runs hot, localized boiling
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect firewall heater hose routing. 2. Ensure bypass loop allows continuous flow if required by OEM circuit. 3. Restore proper U-hose loop.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Water Pump Weep Hole Leak — Bearing Seal Wear
phContext: 80,000+ km sedans/MPVs; gradual coolant loss
symptoms: Pink/green crust below water pump pulley, chirping bearing
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect bottom weep hole of water pump with mirror. 2. Check pulley for radial play with belt off. 3. Replace water pump and timing/drive belt.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Expansion Valve (TXV) Stuck Open/Closed — Poor Cooling
phContext: Cars with fluctuating vent temps and abnormal gauge readings
symptoms: Low-side pressure too high (>55 psi) or vacuum (<5 psi)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check superheat/subcooling on manifold gauges. 2. Feel TXV inlet vs. outlet pipe temps. 3. Replace TXV and receiver-drier, vacuum, and recharge.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Condenser Damaged by Road Stones — Slow Leak
phContext: Highway commuters (NLEX/SLEX/CALAX) without bumper mesh
symptoms: Oily wet spot on lower condenser fins, A/C loses cold over weeks
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect condenser face through lower bumper grille for oily dirt spots. 2. UV-dye or nitrogen leak test. 3. Replace condenser.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Engine Overheats Only at Highway Speed (100+ km/h)
phContext: Missing under-engine splash shield / air dam or collapsed lower hose
symptoms: Cool in city, temp rises steadily on expressway
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect lower radiator hose when revving (soft hose sucks flat without internal spring). 2. Check missing radiator air baffles/undertray. 3. Check radiator internal flow.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Blower Motor Works Only on Speed 4 (Max) — Resistor
phContext: Manual A/C vehicles (Vios E/J, Mirage, L300, Hilux J)
symptoms: Speeds 1, 2, 3 dead; Speed 4 blasts full
diagnosticSteps: 1. Locate blower resistor in evaporator housing near blower. 2. Test thermal fuse and resistor coils for open circuit. 3. Check blower motor amps (high draw blows resistor).

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Insufficient Coolant Temp for Closed Loop — Stuck Thermostat
phContext: Same as P0128 on older OBD-II Toyotas/Mitsubishis
symptoms: High fuel consumption, MIL on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify ECT reaches >80°C within 10 minutes. 2. Replace stuck-open thermostat. 3. Verify ECT sensor accuracy.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Compressor Shaft Seal Leak — Oil Sling on Hood
phContext: Cars sitting unused or aged compressor seals
symptoms: Line of compressor oil slung onto hood insulation above pulley
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect behind A/C clutch pulley with UV light. 2. Check for PAG oil film on fan shroud/hood. 3. Replace shaft seal or compressor.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Coolant Overflow Bottle Cracked — Sun/Heat Embrittlement
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest/EcoSport pressurized degas bottles
symptoms: Coolant leaks down fender liner, bottle micro-cracks under cap
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressurize system and inspect pressurized degas tank seams. 2. Replace tank and pressure cap together. 3. Bleed system.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Ambient Temp Sensor Skewed — Reads -40°C or +60°C
phContext: Front-end bumped cars; sensor behind grille unplugged/damaged
symptoms: Auto climate control blows full hot or won't engage compressor
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check outside temp display on dash/cluster. 2. Inspect 2-pin sensor behind front bumper grille. 3. Measure resistance (~1.5–2.5 kΩ at 30°C).

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Auxiliary Electric Pusher Fan Dead — Overheating on Climbs
phContext: Vans (HiAce, Urvan, L300) with under-seat engine & condenser fans
symptoms: A/C cuts off and engine temp rises in traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect condenser fan(s) under floor/front bumper (exposed to rain/mud). 2. Check dedicated fan relay and fusible link. 3. Replace mud-seized fan motor.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Serrated/Loose A/C Hose Crimp Leak — Vibrating Lines
phContext: Diesel pickups/vans; engine vibration fatiguing hose crimps
symptoms: Oil/dust buildup around aluminum-to-rubber A/C hose crimp
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect high-pressure discharge hose crimps for oily grime. 2. Nitrogen-soap test at 200 psi. 3. Re-crimp or replace hose assembly.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: HVAC Solar/Sunload Sensor Open — Dash Top Sensor
phContext: Automatic climate cars (Fortuner, Montero, Altis); windshield tinting
symptoms: A/C fan speed doesn't ramp up in bright sun (minor effect)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Sunload sensor PID under bright light vs. shade. 2. Check if sensor was left unplugged during dash/tint work. 3. Note: indoor shop shade often sets B1479/B1421.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Coolant Level Sensor Stuck — False Low-Coolant Warning
phContext: Ford, European/Chinese SUVs; magnetic float stuck in degas tank
symptoms: Low coolant warning on dash despite full reservoir
diagnosticSteps: 1. Visually verify coolant level cold. 2. Check 2-pin reed switch at bottom of tank. 3. Clean or replace reservoir with integrated float.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: A/C Smells Like Vinegar / Mold — Wet Evaporator Core
phContext: Humid PH rainy season; drivers turning off car with A/C still wet
symptoms: Sour/musty odor for first 2 minutes of A/C startup
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect cabin filter and drain tube. 2. Perform foam/coil cleaner flush on evaporator core. 3. Advise turning A/C off (fan on) 2 min before parking.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Timing Cover / Water Pump Gasket Seep — Slow Loss
phContext: High-mileage sedans; slow drip evaporating on hot block
symptoms: Coolant reservoir drops 1 cm per week with no puddle on ground
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pressure-test system overnight cold (no evaporation hides leaks!). 2. Use UV dye in coolant to trace weep under timing cover. 3. Reseal pump/cover.

domainName: Engine Cooling & Tropical HVAC / Aircon Load Systems
title: Recirculation Door Broken — Hot Outside Air Mixing In
phContext: Older cars with broken plastic recirc flap link; exhaust fumes enter
symptoms: A/C struggles in traffic, smells Jeepney exhaust inside cabin
diagnosticSteps: 1. Toggle Recirc/Fresh button and listen/inspect flap behind glovebox. 2. Verify servo motor moves flap fully to seal fresh-air cowl. 3. Repair linkage.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: TCM Requested MIL — General Transmission Fault
phContext: All AT/CVT/DCT vehicles; generic engine-side flag
symptoms: Check Engine Light on, AT/CVT warning flashing, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read TCM (Transmission Control Module) directly — P0700 only means 'check TCM'. 2. Record freeze-frame temp and gear. 3. Follow specific TCM DTC.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Secondary Line Pressure Too Low — Worn Pump / Filter
phContext: Mitsubishi Mirage/Outlander, Nissan Almera/Juke (Jatco CVT)
symptoms: Shuddering on takeoff, sluggish acceleration, whine from gearbox
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check CVT fluid level/color (burnt smell = wear). 2. Monitor Primary vs. Secondary pressure PIDs. 3. Drop pan, replace paper cartridge cooler filter + strainer, and inspect magnet for belt flakes.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Torque Converter Clutch (TCC) Stuck Off — Solenoid/Seal
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova AT, Mitsubishi Xpander 4AT, Montero
symptoms: Engine revs higher than normal at 80– 100 km/h, poor highway MPG
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor TCC Lockup Slip RPM PID at steady 80 km/h (should drop near 0 RPM). 2. Command TCC solenoid ON via scan tool. 3. Check ATF condition and valve body lockup valve.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Overheating in Traffic / Mountain Climbs (Baguio/Marcos)
phContext: Honda City/BR-V, Nissan Almera, Mitsubishi Mirage; degraded CVTF
symptoms: CVT temp warning light, car refuses to accelerate (thermal limp mode)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read CVT Fluid Temp PID (often >125–140°C when triggered). 2. Inspect external CVT fluid warmer/cooler lines for blockage. 3. Replace degraded CVTF and clean radiator/cooler.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Judder / Shudder on Light Takeoff (15–30 km/h)
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis CVT, Honda City/Jazz CVT; worn start clutch/fluid
symptoms: Rhythmic vibration accelerating gently from stoplight
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check CVTF service history (must use exact OEM spec: Toyota FE/TC, Honda HCF-2, Mitsubishi J4). 2. Perform 2x drain-and-fill + filter change. 3. Perform CVT start-clutch/pressure calibration.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor (NT) Circuit — Metal Fuzz
phContext: Automatic & CVT cars; magnetic sensor tip coated in clutch/belt debris
symptoms: Harsh shifts, speedometer erratic, stuck in 3rd gear
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare Input Speed (NT) vs. Engine RPM PID in gear. 2. Remove turbine speed sensor and clean iron filings from tip. 3. Measure sensor resistance/5V supply and check wiring.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Output Speed Sensor (NO) Circuit — Broken Wire / Sensor
phContext: Toyota Innova/Fortuner AT, Mitsubishi, Hyundai; underbody harness
symptoms: No upshift past 1st/2nd, speedometer dead, O/D OFF flashes
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor Output Speed PID while driving. 2. Inspect sensor connector near rear of transmission housing. 3. Scope sensor AC/square-wave signal.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Incorrect Gear Ratio — Worn Clutch Packs or Low Fluid
phContext: High-mileage ATs (Vios, Innova, Starex, Adventure/Montero)
symptoms: Engine flares (revs up) between 2nd–3rd or 3rd–4th shifts
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ATF level at proper temp (typically 35–45°C or hot idle per OEM). 2. Inspect fluid for dark brown/burnt odor. 3. Check line pressure and solenoid operation before overhaul.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Shift Solenoid A Malfunction — Open Coil or Sticking Valve
phContext: Toyota 4AT/5AT, Hyundai/Kia AT, Mitsubishi; heat-aged solenoid
symptoms: Stuck in limp gear, hard clunk into Drive/Reverse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure solenoid A resistance at TCM/transmission plug (spec 11–16 ohms or 3–6 ohms per type). 2. Actuate solenoid via scan tool and listen for click. 3. Inspect internal valve body harness.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Shift Solenoid B Malfunction — Internal Harness Break
phContext: Hyundai Accent/Tucson, Kia, Toyota; brittle internal ATF-soaked wires
symptoms: Missing 2nd or 3rd gear, MIL + AT warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Ohm-test Solenoid B from external transmission round plug to ground. 2. Drop transmission pan to inspect internal harness and solenoid connector. 3. Replace solenoid/harness.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck Off — Valve Body Wear
phContext: Toyota 5AT/6AT (Fortuner, Hilux, Innova), Ford 6R80
symptoms: Harsh 2–3 flare or bang, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor line pressure and SLT/SLU solenoid current PIDs. 2. Drop pan and inspect valve body for stuck plunger/debris. 3. Replace linear solenoid and reset TCM memory.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Pressure Control Solenoid D (SLT) Stuck Off
phContext: Toyota 6-speed AT (Hilux/Fortuner/Innova 2016+); varnish/wear
symptoms: Delayed Drive engagement, harsh downshifts, limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ATF level precisely at 35– 45°C check-plug temp. 2. Command SLT solenoid test via Techstream/scan tool. 3. Clean/replace SLT solenoid or valve body.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Clutch Actuator Circuit Open (DCT / AMT) — Brush Wear
phContext: Ford Fiesta/EcoSport PowerShift (DPS6), Suzuki Celerio/S-Presso AGS
symptoms: Transmission Fault message, no-start or stuck in neutral
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check battery voltage (DPS6 is ultra-sensitive to <12.2V!). 2. Swap Clutch Actuator A & B motors to see if fault follows motor. 3. Inspect TCM power/ground and fork binding.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: DCT Clutch A Stuck Engaged — Seized Release Fork
phContext: Ford Fiesta/EcoSport DPS6; dust & rust seizing clutch forks in traffic
symptoms: Violent shuddering, stalls when stopping, cannot select Reverse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Remove clutch actuator motor and turn spline with 14-point tool (must spring back smoothly). 2. If stiff/jammed, remove transmission to clean/replace clutch forks & dual clutch. 3. Update TCM calibration.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: DCT Clutch Overheating Warning in Crawling Traffic
phContext: Ford Territory/EcoSport, Geely Coolray, MG; creeping without full release
symptoms: Dash warning 'Transmission Hot, Stop Safely', juddering takeoff
diagnosticSteps: 1. Teach driver not to creep on hills using throttle (use brake hold/full release). 2. Scan DCT clutch temp PIDs and check for worn clutch friction. 3. Check dual-clutch air vents/fluid.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Transmission Range Sensor (Inhibitor) — Corroded Contacts
phContext: Mitsubishi, Hyundai, Kia, Toyota; water splash on gearbox side
symptoms: Gear indicator blank/wrong, won't crank in Park, harsh engagement
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read PRNDL switch state PIDs while moving shifter slowly. 2. Unplug and inspect 8/10-pin range switch for moisture. 3. Replace or clean switch and align in Neutral.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Transmission Fluid Temp (TFT) Sensor Circuit — Open
phContext: Toyota, Nissan, Hyundai; sensor integrated into internal valve body harness
symptoms: No TCC lockup, late shifts, false overheat warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read TFT PID at cold key-on (should match ambient ~30°C; -40°C = open). 2. Measure TFT thermistor resistance at transmission plug. 3. Replace internal harness.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Switch A Range/Performance
phContext: Honda City/Civic/CR-V (5AT & CVT); clogged pressure switch screen
symptoms: Flashing 'D' light on dash, harsh shifts
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Honda 2nd/3rd clutch pressure switch continuity at KOEO vs. pressure. 2. Clean debris from switch port and test with air pressure. 3. Replace faulty pressure switch.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Flashing 'D' Indicator on Honda — Pressure Switch or Sensor
phContext: Honda City, Jazz, Civic, CR-V; common Honda TCM fault indicator
symptoms: Green 'D' light blinks continuously while driving
diagnosticSteps: 1. Connect scan tool to Honda TCM (blinking D = active TCM DTC). 2. Inspect 2nd/3rd pressure switches or CVT speed sensor. 3. Check ATF DW-1 / HCF-2 level.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Delayed Engagement into Drive/Reverse (2–4 Seconds)
phContext: High-mileage ATs (Vios, Innova, Adventure); hardened piston O-rings
symptoms: Engine revs before transmission clunks into gear, worse when cold
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ATF level and condition. 2. Measure main line pressure at idle in D and R. 3. If pressure builds slowly, internal rubber lip seals are hardened (overhaul required).

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Shifter Stuck in Park — Faulty Shift-Lock Solenoid / Brake Switch
phContext: All automatic PH vehicles; broken brake pedal stopper or solenoid
symptoms: Key turns, engine starts, shifter refuses to move out of P
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if brake lights work (if not, fix brake switch/fuse first!). 2. Use manual shift-lock override button to move car safely. 3. Test 12V to shift-lock solenoid at console.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Shifter Moves Freely, Gear Doesn't Change — Broken Cable Bushing
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis/Innova, Mitsubishi, Ford; brittle nylon bushing
symptoms: Shifter feels loose/floppy, car stuck in Drive or Park
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect shift cable end at transmission lever under hood (or under console). 2. Replace crumbled nylon bushing with OEM or polyurethane bushing. 3. Verify cable adjustment.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: TCC Circuit Intermittent — Worn Lockup Valve / Wiring
phContext: High-mileage ATs; lockup shudder at 60–80 km/h
symptoms: RPM surges +/- 200 RPM at steady cruise, feels like rumble strip
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor TCC slip RPM PID at steady 70 km/h. 2. Replace degraded ATF with OEM fluid. 3. Test lockup solenoid and valve body bore wear.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Secondary Pressure Sensor B Range — Debris/Sensor
phContext: Nissan Almera/Sylphy, Mitsubishi Mirage/ASX
symptoms: Limp mode, sluggish launch
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Secondary Pressure PID at KOEO (must be ~0 MPa). 2. Check 5V/GND/signal at pressure sensor. 3. Flush CVTF and replace sensor if skewed.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Step Motor Circuit (Nissan/Mitsubishi Jatco)
phContext: Nissan Sylphy/Juke/X-Trail, Mitsubishi Lancer/ASX CVT
symptoms: Transmission stuck in low ratio (high RPM, max 60 km/h)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure step motor 4 coils to common pin (spec ~15–25 ohms each). 2. Command step motor steps via scan tool. 3. Drop pan and replace step motor.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Manual Transmission Hard Shifting When Hot — Slave/Master
phContext: Manual Hilux, Ranger, Vios, Mirage; moisture-boiled DOT3/4 fluid
symptoms: Difficult to engage 1st/Reverse in heavy traffic
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check clutch fluid reservoir (black/murky = water & seal wear). 2. Bleed clutch hydraulics completely with fresh DOT4. 3. Inspect master/slave cylinder for internal bypass.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Manual Clutch Pedal Stays on Floor — Blown Concentric Slave
phContext: Ford Ranger, Nissan Navara, newer manual crossovers
symptoms: Sudden loss of clutch pedal, brake fluid dripping from bellhousing
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check brake/clutch reservoir level. 2. Inspect bottom of bellhousing for fresh brake fluid leak. 3. Remove transmission to replace Concentric Slave Cylinder (CSC) & clutch.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Dual-Mass Flywheel (DMF) Rattle — Diesel Manual Pickups
phContext: Ford Ranger, Nissan Navara, Isuzu; worn internal DMF springs
symptoms: Metallic clatter at idle that disappears when pressing clutch pedal
diagnosticSteps: 1. Listen at bellhousing at idle vs. clutch depressed. 2. Check crankshaft end-play and DMF rotational freeplay (>2–3 teeth = worn). 3. Replace DMF with clutch kit.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: TCM Power Input Signal Low — Corroded TCM Fuse/Relay
phContext: Hyundai/Kia, Ford, Mitsubishi; loose fuse or ground
symptoms: Transmission locked in 3rd/4th limp gear, multiple comms errors
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check TCM 15A/20A IG1 and B+ fuses. 2. Load-test TCM power and ground pins at connector. 3. Inspect engine bay splice.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Lost Communication with TCM — Broken CAN Wire at Gearbox
phContext: Pickups/SUVs; underbody harness rubbing frame crossmember
symptoms: Gear display blank, no crank or limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure CAN-H/L resistance at TCM plug (60 ohms) and 12V/GND. 2. Inspect harness routing over bellhousing/crossmember for rub-through. 3. Repair twisted CAN pair.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Wrong ATF Used (Dexron III in WS/CVT) — Instant Shudder
phContext: Vehicles serviced at generic gas stations using 'universal' fluid
symptoms: Harsh shifting, shuddering, overheating within days of service
diagnosticSteps: 1. Confirm exact OEM fluid spec (e.g., Toyota WS, Nissan NS-3, Honda HCF-2). 2. Perform full 100% fluid flush/exchange immediately. 3. Reset TCM adaptive learn values.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Input Speed Sensor No Signal — Open Hall Sensor
phContext: Hyundai/Kia 6AT, Nissan CVT; internal sensor failure
symptoms: Stuck in single gear, harsh shifts, speed sensor PID = 0
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 12V/5V supply at input sensor connector. 2. Scope signal wire while wheels/engine turn. 3. Replace input speed sensor.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Output Speed Sensor No Signal — Rear Driveshaft/Hub
phContext: Toyota/Mitsubishi/Hyundai AT; open sensor coil
symptoms: No upshift from 1st, speedometer may read 0
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check Output Speed PID while rolling. 2. Measure sensor resistance (if VR) or 5V/12V (if Hall). 3. Inspect connector above transmission tailhousing.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
phContext: High-mileage ATs; shorted solenoid coil or pinched wire
symptoms: Very harsh shifts (max line pressure failsafe)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug transmission main connector; measure solenoid A resistance to ground. 2. Check internal harness for insulation cracked by hot ATF. 3. Replace solenoid/harness.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Speed Sensor / Function Fault (Nissan)
phContext: Nissan Almera/Urvan/Navara; CVT limp mode trigger
symptoms: Engine revs sluggishly, CVT warning
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Nissan-specific TCM sub-codes (P0715, P0720, P0868). 2. Check ABS wheel speed signals (TCM uses ABS speed via CAN). 3. Inspect CVTF level.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: CVT Whining Noise Increasing with Engine RPM
phContext: High-mileage Mirage/Almera/Vios; worn primary pulley bearings
symptoms: High-pitched whine at 40–80 km/h even in Neutral coasting
diagnosticSteps: 1. Use chassis ears/stethoscope on CVT case vs. alternator/wheel bearings. 2. Drain fluid to check for bearing metal flakes. 3. Overhaul CVT pulley bearings.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Automatic Transmission Oil Leak at Drive Axle Seal
phContext: Front-wheel drive cars (Vios, City, Mirage, Xpander) hitting lubak
symptoms: Red/amber oil drips under gearbox, low fluid slipping
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect left and right CV axle output seals for wet oil sling. 2. Check axle play in differential carrier bearings. 3. Replace axle seal and top up OEM ATF/CVTF.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Transmission Range Sensor Range/Performance — Misadjusted
phContext: Vehicles after transmission removal/install
symptoms: Intermittent limp mode, gear indicator flickers between D and N
diagnosticSteps: 1. Loosen range switch mounting bolts, put shifter in N, align OEM index mark/pin. 2. Verify PID shows exact single gear per detent. 3. Check shifter cable tension.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: 4x4 Transfer Case Chain Stretch — Clunk on Takeoff
phContext: Older 4x4 pickups/SUVs; loud bang under floor in 4H
symptoms: Ratcheting clunk under center console under heavy torque in 4WD
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test in 2H vs. 4H on loose gravel. 2. Drain transfer case oil to inspect for aluminum shavings. 3. Replace stretched transfer case chain.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Shift Error (Generic) — Slipping Clutch / Low Pressure
phContext: Hyundai/Kia, Mitsubishi; actual gear ratio doesn't match commanded
symptoms: Flare during 3–4 upshift, enters limp mode
diagnosticSteps: 1. Graph Input RPM vs. Output RPM x Gear Ratio during shift. 2. Check ATF level and line pressure. 3. Inspect valve body accumulator springs and clutches.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Clutch Position Control Error (AMT/AGS)
phContext: Suzuki Celerio/S-Presso/Dzire AGS; worn clutch or actuator fluid
symptoms: Gear light flashes, won't shift into 1st or Reverse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check AGS hydraulic reservoir fluid level. 2. Read clutch stroke PIDs and perform clutch kiss-point learn. 3. Inspect clutch disc wear.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Clutch Chatter on Cold Morning Takeoff — Glazed Flywheel
phContext: Manual Vios/Mirage/L300 in stop-and-go delivery service
symptoms: Whole car shakes when releasing clutch in 1st gear
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect engine/transmission rubber mounts first (torn mounts mimic chatter). 2. Check for oil contamination from rear main seal. 3. Resurface flywheel and replace clutch.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio — Sprag / Low Clutch Slip
phContext: High-mileage ATs; car barely moves in D1, moves in L/1st
symptoms: Slips heavily on takeoff, normal once in 2nd/3rd
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test manual 'L' or '1' position (engages coast clutch bypassing sprag). 2. Check ATF for burnt clutch material. 3. Rebuild transmission low/reverse clutch or one-way sprag.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio — 3rd Clutch Drum Seal Leak
phContext: Older Honda/Toyota/Mitsubishi 4AT; worn direct clutch piston
symptoms: Engine flares sharply at 40–50 km/h on 2– 3 shift
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify shift solenoid states during 2– 3 command. 2. Check fluid for dark burnt grit. 3. Air-check clutch drums during overhaul.

domainName: Automatic, CVT & Dual-Clutch Transmission (AT / CVT / DCT)
title: TCM Adaptive Reset Needed After Battery / Rebuild
phContext: Toyota, Honda, Mitsubishi, Ford; harsh shifting after repair
symptoms: Harsh upshifts/downshifts despite healthy hardware
diagnosticSteps: 1. Perform TCM Reset Memory / Adaptive Clear via diagnostic tool. 2. Execute OEM drive cycle (gentle accelerations at 20–30% throttle through all gears). 3. Verify smooth shifts.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit — Broken Wire
phContext: Toyota Vios, Honda City, Mitsubishi Xpander; suspension travel flexing wire
symptoms: ABS + VSC + Brake warning lights on, ABS disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Graph all 4 wheel speed PIDs during 20 km/h test drive (FL reads 0). 2. Measure sensor resistance (1.0–1.6 kΩ if VR) or 12V/5V bias (if active Hall). 3. Wiggle-test harness inside wheel well.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Right Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit — Debris / Gap
phContext: Pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Ranger, Montero) after off-road or mud
symptoms: False ABS pulsation just before stopping on dry pavement
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scope sensor output while spinning wheel by hand (check for weak/erratic amplitude). 2. Inspect sensor tip for iron filings or bent tone ring tooth. 3. Verify wheel bearing play.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor — Rear Axle Oil Leak
phContext: Rear-wheel-drive pickups/SUVs (Hilux, Fortuner, Navara); diff oil on tone ring
symptoms: ABS light on, wet gear oil around rear brake backing plate
diagnosticSteps: 1. Pull rear wheel speed sensor and check for differential gear oil contamination. 2. Replace leaking rear axle shaft oil seal and clean tone ring. 3. Test sensor signal.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Right Rear Wheel Speed Sensor — Rat Bite / Road Debris
phContext: Cars parked outdoors; rear subframe wiring chewed or snagged
symptoms: ABS + Traction light on, speedometer may drop if RR-referenced
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect rear axle/trailing-arm harness for chew marks or stone cuts. 2. Check continuity from sensor plug to ABS module connector. 3. Splice with waterproof heat-shrink.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Toyota Right Front Speed Sensor Signal Malfunction
phContext: Toyota Vios/Innova/Hilux/Fortuner; rusted/swollen hub bearing encoder
symptoms: ABS activates unnecessarily at <15 km/h, then sets C0200
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check wheel bearing axial play (worn bearing increases air gap). 2. Inspect magnetic encoder strip on hub seal for rust delamination. 3. Replace hub bearing or sensor.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Toyota Right Rear Speed Sensor — Corroded Rear Hub Plug
phContext: Toyota Vios/Altis/Yaris (rear disc/drum hub integrated sensor)
symptoms: ABS + Brake light on after heavy rain
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug 2-pin connector on rear hub carrier and check for water/green pins. 2. Test harness voltage (12V/2.5V reference). 3. Replace rear hub bearing assembly if internal sensor failed.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Ford/Mazda Wheel Speed Sensor Signal — Aftermarket Bearing
phContext: Ford Ranger/Everest/EcoSport; bearing installed backwards or non-magnetic
symptoms: ABS light on immediately after wheel bearing replacement
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify magnetic encoder ring faces the sensor (test with magnetic viewing card). 2. Check sensor gap and wiring. 3. Reinstall bearing with encoder side inward.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ABS Hydraulic Pump Motor Circuit — Stuck Brushes
phContext: Ford Fiesta/Focus/Ranger, Hyundai, Mitsubishi; seldom-activated pump
symptoms: ABS light on solid, pump won't run during scan tool bleed test
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 40A/60A ABS pump fusible link. 2. Command ABS pump motor ON via scan tool while tapping motor gently. 3. Check ABS module ground strap; rebuild/replace pump motor.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ECU Internal Malfunction (ABS) — Solder Cracks / Heat
phContext: Older SUVs/vans; underhood ABS module exposed to engine heat
symptoms: ABS light on, no comm or permanent internal valve/pump DTC
diagnosticSteps: 1. Verify all ABS power (KL30 x2, KL15) and ground pins under halogen bulb load. 2. If powers/grounds are 100% solid, inspect ABS ECU PCB for cracked pump solder pins. 3. Reflow or replace ABS unit.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Toyota Low/High Power Supply Voltage — Weak Battery/Alt
phContext: Toyota Vios/Fortuner/Hilux; aging battery or loose terminal
symptoms: ABS/VSC lights turn on at idle with A/C + headlights
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check charging voltage (must be 13.5–14.5V) and battery CCA. 2. Inspect ABS 1 & ABS 2 fuses in engine bay box. 3. Clear C1241 once charging is restored.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Steering Angle Sensor (SAS) Circuit — Needs Calibration
phContext: Hyundai, Kia, Mitsubishi, Toyota; after wheel alignment or battery change
symptoms: ESC/VSC light on, steering wheel off-center
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read SAS angle PID with wheels straight ahead (must be 0° +/- 3°). 2. Perform mechanical alignment first if steering wheel is crooked. 3. Run SAS Zero-Point Calibration via scan tool.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Pressure Transducer Fault — Contaminated Brake Fluid
phContext: Ford, Hyundai, Mitsubishi; dark/wet DOT3/4 fluid corroding internal sensor
symptoms: ESC/Stability light on, hill-start assist disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Brake Pressure PID at rest (must be ~0 bar, rises smoothly on pedal press). 2. Flush dark moisture-laden brake fluid. 3. Replace ABS HCU/pressure sensor if stuck.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Pump Motor Circuit Malfunction — Blown ABS Fuse
phContext: Nissan, Suzuki, Mitsubishi; shorted ABS pump motor
symptoms: ABS light on, blown 30A/40A ABS Motor fuse
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug ABS module and test pump motor pins for short to chassis. 2. Replace blown fusible link only after verifying no short. 3. Repair/replace ABS pump.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ABS/TCS Solenoid Valve Open/Short — Moisture in Connector
phContext: Pickups/SUVs; large multi-pin ABS plug under hood wet from engine wash
symptoms: ABS light on, specific inlet/outlet valve DTC
diagnosticSteps: 1. Unplug main ABS harness connector (release cam lock carefully) and inspect for water/verdigris. 2. Dry with compressed air and contact cleaner. 3. Verify valve coil continuity if internal.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Pedal Sinks Slowly at Stoplight — Master Cylinder Bypass
phContext: High-mileage sedans/taxis; worn primary cup seals from dirty fluid
symptoms: Pedal creeps to floor while holding foot at traffic light, no external leak
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect all 4 calipers/wheel cylinders for leaks first. 2. Pinch/cap master cylinder ports briefly to confirm internal bypass. 3. Replace brake master cylinder and bleed with fresh DOT4.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Hard Brake Pedal / Poor Stopping — Torn Booster Vacuum Hose
phContext: Gasoline cars (cracked booster hose) or Diesel vacuum pump failure
symptoms: Pedal feels rock-hard, requires heavy leg force to stop
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check intake manifold vacuum (gas) or alternator-mounted vacuum pump (diesel, -75 kPa). 2. Listen for hissing under dash (torn booster diaphragm). 3. Replace check valve, hose, or booster.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Pulsation / Steering Shake at High Speed — Warped Rotors
phContext: Mountain descents (Kennon/Marcos/Tagaytay ) + splashing through puddles
symptoms: Steering wheel shudders when braking from 80+ km/h
diagnosticSteps: 1. Measure front rotor lateral runout with dial indicator (spec <0.05 mm) and thickness variation. 2. Check for seized caliper slide pins causing uneven pad heat. 3. Resurface or replace rotors.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Dragging Brake / Hot Wheel — Seized Caliper Slide Pins
phContext: Cars driven in rain/floods; washed-out silicone grease on pins
symptoms: Car pulls to one side, wheel hub scorching hot, poor MPG
diagnosticSteps: 1. Raise wheel and spin by hand; crack bleeder screw (if wheel frees, rubber brake hose is collapsed internally). 2. Disassemble caliper slide pins, clean rust, and lubricate with silicone pin grease. 3. Rebuild sticking piston.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Zero Point Calibration of Deceleration Sensor Undone (Toyota)
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner/Vios/Innova; after ABS reset or battery swap
symptoms: VSC/TRAC light blinking or solid with no hardware fault
diagnosticSteps: 1. Park vehicle on completely flat, level floor with steering centered. 2. Run ABS/VSC Zero-Point Calibration via scan tool (or Ts/CG pin procedure). 3. Verify Yaw/G-sensor PIDs read 0.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Steering Position Signal Malfunction — Clock Spring / SAS
phContext: Nissan Navara/Almera, Mitsubishi; after rack/tie-rod replacement
symptoms: VDC/Slip light on continuously
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check SAS PID while turning lock-to-lock (must count smoothly without freezing). 2. Inspect SAS optical/magnetic disc and 5V/CAN supply. 3. Recalibrate or replace SAS.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Electronic Parking Brake (EPB) Actuator Open — Rear Caliper
phContext: Honda Civic/CR-V, Ford Territory, BYD, modern SUVs; chafed rear wire
symptoms: EPB light flashing, parking brake stuck ON or won't engage
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect 2-pin motor connector on rear brake caliper for torn wire from road debris. 2. Test EPB motor with 12V fused jumper (reverses polarity to retract). 3. Run EPB service mode calibration.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: EPB Won't Release — Low Battery or Stuck Rear Pad
phContext: EPB-equipped vehicles parked with weak 12V battery
symptoms: Grinding click, EPB warning, rear wheels locked
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check battery voltage (EPB motors draw 15–20A each; <11.5V stalls them). 2. Apply jumper battery and cycle EPB switch while pressing brake pedal. 3. Inspect seized rear caliper.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Lateral Acceleration / Yaw Rate Sensor Fault
phContext: SUVs/sedans with center-console G-sensor exposed to spilled drinks/flood
symptoms: ESC/VSC light on, traction control disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Yaw Rate & Lateral G PIDs at standstill (must be ~0 deg/s and 0.0 G). 2. Inspect sensor under center console/front seat for coffee spill or flood silt. 3. Replace and calibrate.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Fluid Boiling / Spongy Pedal Descending Baguio/Tagaytay
phContext: Vehicles with >3-year-old DOT3 fluid (high moisture absorption in PH humidity)
symptoms: Pedal goes soft/to floor after repeated downhill braking
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test brake fluid moisture % with electronic tester (>3% water = unsafe!). 2. Flush entire brake system including ABS bleed routine with fresh DOT4. 3. Advise engine braking on descents.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Speed Sensor Rotor/Tone Ring Damaged — Pothole / Prybar
phContext: Vehicles after wheel bearing/axle service; bent or cracked ABS ring
symptoms: ABS activates randomly at low speed, C0200/C1237 stored
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect tone ring teeth through sensor hole for missing tooth or crack. 2. Scope wheel speed waveform (missing tooth causes sudden voltage drop gap). 3. Replace tone ring/CV axle.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Left Rear Wheel Speed Sensor Range/Performance — Mismatched Tires
phContext: Vehicles running spare donut tire or mismatched tire sizes front/rear
symptoms: ABS/ESC lights turn on above 60 km/h
diagnosticSteps: 1. Compare all 4 tire sizes and inflation pressures! 2. Graph all 4 wheel speeds at steady 60 km/h (one reading >5% different triggers fault). 3. Install matching tire size.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Parking Brake Handbrake Lever High / Weak Hold
phContext: Manual & AT cars (Vios, Mirage, Innova); stretched cables or rear shoes
symptoms: Car rolls on incline even with handbrake pulled 10+ clicks
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect rear drum brake shoe thickness and auto-adjuster star wheel. 2. Adjust rear shoes first, then set cable slack at lever (spec 5–7 clicks). 3. Replace seized parking brake cable.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ECM Communication Circuit (ABS) — Vehicle Model Variant Mismatch
phContext: Used/swapped ABS module or ECU installed without coding
symptoms: VSC/ABS lights on, C1203/U0100
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check VIN/variant coding inside ABS module vs. vehicle spec (2WD vs. 4WD, AT vs. MT). 2. Reprogram/code ABS module to exact chassis spec. 3. Run zero-point calibration.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Invalid Data Received from Vehicle Dynamics Control
phContext: Hyundai/Kia, Ford, Nissan; SAS or G-sensor uncalibrated
symptoms: ESC/ABS lights on, hill-descent disabled
diagnosticSteps: 1. Scan ABS/ESC module for underlying sensor DTCs. 2. Check CAN bus integrity and battery voltage. 3. Calibrate SAS and Yaw/G sensors.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Loud Grinding Noise When Braking — Metal-on-Metal Pads
phContext: Heavy traffic commuters; worn inner brake pad (outer pad still looks okay)
symptoms: Harsh metallic scraping, ruined rotor, low brake fluid level
diagnosticSteps: 1. Always inspect BOTH inner and outer pads (seized slide pin wears inner pad first). 2. Replace pads and resurface/replace scored rotors. 3. Lubricate slide pins.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Master Cylinder Pressure Sensor Malfunction (Toyota)
phContext: Toyota Hilux/Fortuner/Innova/Vios; brake switch or internal pressure sensor
symptoms: ABS/VSC lights on, brake lights may stay on or off
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Master Cylinder Pressure PID at rest (0 MPa) and pressed (3–10 MPa). 2. Check Stop Light Switch operation first (causes false correlation). 3. Inspect ABS actuator connector.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Open/Short in ABS Solenoid Relay Circuit
phContext: Toyota/Mitsubishi; corroded internal relay or blown ABS SOL fuse
symptoms: ABS light on, pump/valves inoperative
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check ABS NO.1 / ABS SOL fuse (30A–50A) in engine bay. 2. Verify B+ reaches ABS connector pins under load. 3. Replace ABS actuator if relay is internal and open.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Booster Hissing Inside Cabin — Torn Vacuum Seal
phContext: Older sedans/MPVs; air leak at brake pedal pushrod boot
symptoms: Hissing stops when pressing brake pedal, rough idle (vacuum leak!)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Listen under driver dash while pressing/releasing brake pedal. 2. Spray/smoke around booster rear seal; watch LTFT fuel trim. 3. Replace brake booster assembly.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ABS Acceleration Sensor / G-Sensor Circuit (Nissan/Hyundai)
phContext: 4WD pickups/SUVs; sensor under console or rusted bracket
symptoms: ABS + 4WD + Slip lights on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check G-sensor 5V, GND, and signal PID (~2.5V flat). 2. Inspect connector under center console. 3. Replace sensor and run calibration.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Soft Brake Pedal After Pad Replacement — Air or Unseated Caliper
phContext: DIY/roadside brake job where bleeder was opened or caliper swapped sides
symptoms: Pedal goes halfway down before biting
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check caliper bleeder screw orientation (bleeder MUST be at the very top of caliper!). 2. Pressure-bleed all 4 corners starting farthest from master cylinder. 3. Run scan-tool ABS bleed.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ABS Pump Motor Control — Ground Strap Corrosion
phContext: SUVs/cars with ABS ground bolted to painted fender apron
symptoms: Intermittent ABS light over bumps, pump slows down
diagnosticSteps: 1. Locate ABS ground lug on inner fender/frame rail. 2. Measure voltage drop from ABS ground pin to battery negative during pump test (<0.2V). 3. Clean to bare metal and torque.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Steering Angle Sensor Reverse/Zero Error — Rack Alignment
phContext: Hyundai/Kia/Mitsubishi; tie rods adjusted unequally
symptoms: ESC activates unexpectedly on gentle highway curves!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check steering wheel centering and SAS PID at straight-ahead drive. 2. Perform 4-wheel alignment with steering centered, then reset SAS zero-point. 3. Test drive.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Brake Light Switch Causing Limp Mode / No Cruise
phContext: Pickups/SUVs; ECM cuts throttle when brake + gas pressed simultaneously
symptoms: Sudden power cut when hitting bumps (bouncy brake pedal)
diagnosticSteps: 1. Monitor Brake Switch 1 & 2 PIDs while tapping brake pedal lightly. 2. Adjust switch clearance so slight vibration doesn't trigger brake signal. 3. Replace worn switch.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: ABS/TCS Brake Switch Circuit — Blown Stop Fuse
phContext: All ABS/ESC cars; shorted trailer/tail light blowing STOP fuse
symptoms: ABS + ESC lights on, no brake lights, shifter stuck in Park
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 10A/15A STOP fuse (often shares feed with aftermarket third brake light/LEDs). 2. Inspect tail light sockets for melted/shorted bulbs. 3. Replace fuse and switch.

domainName: ABS, EBD, ESC/VSC & Wheel Speed / Braking Electronics
title: Rear Proportioning Valve (LSPV) Seized — Rear Lockup
phContext: Older Hilux, L300, Crosswind, Tamaraw FX with load-sensing valve
symptoms: Rear wheels lock up easily on wet roads when unladen
diagnosticSteps: 1. Inspect LSPV lever arm above rear axle for rust seizure. 2. Bleed LSPV bleeder nipple. 3. Lubricate or replace LSPV and adjust spring height.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS Power Supply Relay Fault — Overheated Column ECU
phContext: Toyota Vios/Yaris/Wigo/Altis; heavy parking lot steering in heat
symptoms: EPS light on, steering suddenly becomes rock-hard
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check 50A/60A EPS fuse in engine bay. 2. Measure 12V IG1 and B+ at EPS ECU under load. 3. Inspect Toyota EPS ECU internal relay solder joints or replace EPS ECU.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS Torque Sensor Circuit — Worn Steering Column Sensor
phContext: Toyota Vios/Avanza, Suzuki Ertiga, Hyundai; steering pulls or shudders
symptoms: EPS light on, steering pulls hard to one side by itself!
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read Torque Sensor 1 & 2 PIDs at rest (must be ~2.5V each) and turning left/right. 2. Check 5V/GND to torque sensor. 3. Replace column torque sensor and perform zero-point learn.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS PIG Power Supply Voltage Low — Weak Battery/Ground
phContext: Modern EPS cars with aging battery or loose terminal
symptoms: EPS light flashes during cranking or idle with A/C on
diagnosticSteps: 1. Test battery voltage and alternator output (EPS draws up to 60–80A at full lock!). 2. Check EPS ground bolt under dash/kick-panel. 3. Clear DTC after fixing 12V supply.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS Steering Column Clunk Over Potholes — Worn Coupler
phContext: Hyundai Accent/Elantra/Tucson, Kia Rio/Picanto; disintegrated rubber star
symptoms: Metallic clunk when jiggling steering wheel left-right or hitting lubak
diagnosticSteps: 1. Turn wheel back and forth with engine off; listen at column motor housing. 2. Drop steering column motor and inspect shredded rubber MDPS flexible coupler. 3. Replace coupler and re-calibrate.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS CAN Time-Out (Hyundai/Kia) — Missing RPM Signal
phContext: Hyundai Accent/Eon/Reina, Kia Picanto/Soluto
symptoms: EPS light on, steering heavy, tach may drop
diagnosticSteps: 1. Check if Engine ECM is running and sending RPM over CAN. 2. Measure CAN-H/L at MDPS ECU (60 ohms). 3. Inspect engine-to-dash CAN connector.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: EPS Thermal Protection Shutdown — Extended Dry Parking
phContext: Drivers dry-steering repeatedly in tight PH mall parking garages
symptoms: Steering turns heavy after 2 min of maneuvering, recovers after 10 min cool-down
diagnosticSteps: 1. Read EPS Motor Temp / Current PIDs (often >110°C thermal cutback). 2. Check battery voltage (low voltage increases motor heat/current). 3. Advise rolling slightly while steering.

domainName: Electric Power Steering (EPS), SRS Airbag & Restraints
title: Driver Front Airbag Squib Open — Broken Clock Spring
phContext: High-mileage Vios, City, Mirage, Hilux; worn spiral cable ribbon
symptoms: SRS Airbag light solid on dash, horn/steering buttons may also fail
